statement: statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITION CIRCUITS. Let L⊆{0,1}^N. At depth t, let the states be the r_t distinct residual languages R_t(p)={z:pz∈L}. For each t<N and input bit b, the transition from these states to the r_{t+1} residual states has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most 2r_t r_{t+1} AND/OR gates, given one-hot state input. Thus all position-specific transitions have total size at most 2∑_{t=0}^{N−1}r_t r_{t+1}. Proof: For each depth-t residual R, its b-section {z:bz∈R} is a unique depth-(t+1) residual, so the transition is a well-defined function f_b:[r_t]→[r_{t+1}]. For each target state j, output the OR of the one-hot input bits i for which f_b(i)=j. Implement each selected term with an AND gate and its OR with at most one fewer OR gates than terms. Across targets there are r_t terms total, hence at most r_t AND and r_t OR gates, bounded by 2r_t≤2r_t r_{t+1} since r_{t+1}≥1. This produces the exact next one-hot state. Applying the construction independently at every layer and for both input bits gives the stated bound per bit-symbol transition and total.

statement: statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITIONS WITH EXACT OR COST. Let L be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N and let r_t be the number of distinct residuals after prefixes of length t. Encode each depth-t residual by a one-hot vector of length r_t. For each t<N and input bit b, the next one-hot vector is computable using at most max(r_t-1,0) fan-in-two OR gates; across both symbols and all positions the total is at most 2*sum_{t=0}^{N-1} max(r_t-1,0). Proof: each source residual has exactly one b-section, which is a depth-(t+1) residual. For each target coordinate j, OR together the source coordinates whose b-section is j. If k_j sources map to j, this uses max(k_j-1,0) OR gates (zero for empty, one for singleton). Since every source maps to exactly one target, sum_j k_j=r_t, and the total is sum_j max(k_j-1,0) <= max(r_t-1,0). The resulting vector is exactly one-hot because each source one-hot vector maps to one target. Summing over b and t gives the bound. The empty language has one empty residual at every level and each transition is the identity on its sole one-hot coordinate, costing zero gates, also covered by the formula.

statement:
statement: EXPLICIT CIRCUIT-LIST PREFIX RECOGNIZER. Let A be the finite set of ordered fan-in-two Boolean circuit descriptions on n inputs with at most s gates, M=|A|. Maintain q_C in {0,1} for every C in A, initialized to 1. At position i, on bit b, update q_C := q_C AND [C(1,...,i-1,b,0,...,0)=b], where the bracket is the fixed truth-table bit of C at position i. Accept iff OR_{C in A} q_C=1. This recognizes exactly prefixes extendible to a truth table in A. Each position-specific transition takes at most M two-input AND gates and acceptance at most max(M-1,0) OR gates. If gate j has at most n+j available wires, then M <= sum_{k=0}^s product_{j=0}^{k-1}(2(n+j)^2+n+j+2).
derivation: For each C, induction on prefix length shows q_C=1 exactly when the first t truth-table bits of C equal the read prefix. The invariant holds at t=0. At the next position the update preserves q_C exactly when C's fixed truth-table bit there equals the received bit, proving the invariant at t+1. Therefore some q_C is 1 exactly when some listed circuit extends the prefix. The transition uses one AND per C with a position-and-circuit-dependent constant. The acceptance OR uses a binary tree. To bound M, count each exact gate count k by encoding each gate as one of two binary operations on an ordered pair of at most n+j wires, one of n+j wires, or one of two constants; sum these products for k=0 through s. This is an explicit-list construction only and gives no polynomial-in-s bound.

statement:
statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITION CIRCUIT. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. At level t<N, let R_t be the distinct residual sets R_t(p)={z: pz in F}, and let d_t=|R_t|. With one-hot input encoding of R in R_t, the map (R,b) -> R_b={u: bu in R}, encoded in R_{t+1}, is computed correctly on valid states by a fan-in-two circuit with at most 4d_t gates, with constants free.
derivation: For each source R in R_t and bit b, let dest(R,b)=R_b in R_{t+1}. For each destination S and bit b, form g_{S,b}=OR_{R:dest(R,b)=S} e_R, using a binary OR tree; empty groups yield constant 0. Since each source has exactly one destination for each b, the total number of OR gates across all groups for a fixed b is at most d_t, and across both b values at most 2d_t. Form h_{S,b}=g_{S,b} AND [input bit equals b], using at most 2d_{t+1} gates naively, but only destinations reached by at least one source need a gate; their count for each b is at most d_t, hence at most 2d_t such gates. Finally y_S=h_{S,0} OR h_{S,1}, using at most d_{t+1} gates, and d_{t+1}<=2d_t because every next-level residual is a section of some level-t residual, each of which has two sections. Total is at most 2d_t+2d_t+2d_t=6d_t, so the asserted 4d_t bound needs refinement. A valid bound of 6d_t follows from this construction. On a valid one-hot input exactly one source R is active, so exactly the coordinate for R_b is output as 1. Therefore replace the stated 4d_t bound with 6d_t before treating the claim as established.
scope: Canonical residual automaton of an arbitrary finite language at one fixed level, with one-hot state encoding and fixed level-dependent transitions. Does not bound d_t in terms of circuit size and does not give a representation map from arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

statement:
statement: Corrected one-hot residual transition bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N, 0<=t<N, and let R_t be the distinct residuals after length-t prefixes, with d_t=|R_t|. The transition (R,b)->R_b, encoded one-hot, is computable on valid states by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most 7d_t gates, counting NOT gates and treating constants and wires as free.
derivation: For each destination S in R_{t+1} and bit b, let E_{S,b}={R in R_t:R_b=S}. Form g_{S,b}=OR_{R in E_{S,b}} e_R, using zero for an empty group. Across all (S,b), the OR trees use at most 2d_t gates, since each source contributes exactly one edge for each bit and an OR tree on k inputs uses at most k-1 gates. Form h_{S,b}=g_{S,b} AND (b=b), where the bit literal is b for b=1 and NOT b for b=0. The groups with nonempty E_{S,b} number at most 2d_t, so these AND gates cost at most 2d_t; one shared NOT gate supplies NOT b. For every S, output y_S=h_{S,0} OR h_{S,1}, using d_{t+1} gates. Every next-level residual is a section of a previous residual, so d_{t+1}<=2d_t. Total is at most 2d_t+2d_t+1+2d_t=6d_t+1<=7d_t, since d_t>=1. On a valid one-hot input exactly one source coordinate is active, so exactly the coordinate for R_b is output. This proves the corrected bound; it does not imply a bound on d_t from a circuit description or a transition simulation for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: statement: WITNESS-ENUMERATION EXT STREAMING LEMMA. Let r,h,N be nonnegative integers and let H_i:{0,1}^r->{0,1} for i=1,...,N each be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most h gates. Let L={x in {0,1}^N: exists w in {0,1}^r such that x_i=H_i(w) for every i}. There is an exact deterministic prefix recognizer for L with 2^r state bits and, at position i, a transition circuit of at most O(2^r(h+1)) gates; the initial state is all ones and acceptance is the OR of the state bits. Proof: index state bits q_w by all w in {0,1}^r. At each position i, set q'_w=q_w AND (x_i iff H_i(w)). Compute H_i(w) with a separate copy of its at-most-h-gate circuit for each w, then combine with x_i and prior q_w using O(1) gates per w. Inductively, after t bits q_w=1 exactly when the first t bits equal H_1(w),...,H_t(w); hence some q_w remains 1 iff the prefix extends to a word in L. The accepting OR uses O(2^r) gates. This is an explicit transition-cost upper bound for a witness relation; it does not imply a lower bound or a relation to an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit C.

statement:
statement: FIXED-CIRCUIT LOCAL VERIFIER AND PREFIX PROJECTION. Let C be a Boolean circuit with N input bits, h fan-in-two gates in topological order, and one output. There is a {AND,OR,NOT} circuit H_C(x,y), with O(h) gates, where y lists one bit per gate, such that H_C(x,y)=1 iff y gives the consistent gate evaluation of C on x and the output is 1. For any prefix p of length t and next bit b, define E_C(p)=1 iff there exist z in {0,1}^{N-t} and y with H_C(pz,y)=1. Then E_C(pb)=1 iff there exist z' in {0,1}^{N-t-1} and y with H_C(pb z',y)=1. The relation circuit in the latter expression is obtained by substituting the fixed prefix bits in H_C, so it has no more gates than H_C. Proof: For each gate i, its local condition y_i=f_i(a_i,b_i) is a Boolean relation on at most three bits and therefore has a constant-size {AND,OR,NOT} circuit. Conjoin the h local conditions and the assertion that the output wire is 1 using O(h) additional gates. By induction in topological order, the local conditions force y to be exactly the circuit evaluation, so H_C accepts precisely accepting computations. Substituting fixed input bits adds no gates. Finally, write the remaining suffix as b z'; this gives the stated child projection identity. This lemma only constructs the local verifier and its exact prefix projection; it gives no small ordinary circuit for eliminating the existential variables and no transition-cost bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: FINITE EXHAUSTIVE CHECK OF EXISTENTIAL COFACTOR IDENTITY. For all Boolean relations H:{0,1}^2×{0,1}→{0,1}, every prefix p of length t<2, next bit b, and remaining suffix z, the projected predicate L(x)=∃w H(x,w) satisfies L(pb z)=∃w H(pb z,w). statement: EXPLICIT WITNESS-ENUMERATION CIRCUIT BOUND. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates, with constants and input wiring free, and let G(x)=∨_{w∈{0,1}^r}H(x,w). Then G has a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^r(h+1)−1 gates. For any fixed prefix p, the cofactor G_p has a circuit within the same bound, and fixing a further input bit to form G_{pb} adds no gates.
derivation: For each of the 2^r assignments w, make a separate copy of the h-gate circuit H and hardwire its witness inputs to w; this computes x↦H(x,w) using at most h gates. Combine the 2^r branch outputs with a binary OR tree, which uses 2^r−1 fan-in-two OR gates. Thus the total is at most 2^r h+(2^r−1)=2^r(h+1)−1. Hardwiring any visible input prefix into this circuit preserves its function on the remaining inputs and cannot increase its gate count. Hardwiring the next input bit likewise yields the next cofactor without adding gates. The argument proves an explicit exponential upper bound and makes no polynomial-size assertion when r grows.

label: S0821
statement:
statement: FIXED-CIRCUIT TABLEAU PROJECTION LEMMA. Let C be a fixed acyclic Boolean circuit with g fan-in-at-most-two gates in topological order, and let y_1,...,y_g be Boolean variables for its gate outputs. Let H_C(x,y) assert the correct local Boolean equation for every gate and that C's output is 1. Then for every input x, there is exactly one y satisfying all gate equations, and ∃y H_C(x,y)=1 iff C(x)=1. H_C has size O(g) in fan-in-two Boolean gates when constants and wiring are free. Proof: Induct on gate order. Once x and y_1,...,y_{i-1} are fixed, gate i's local equation forces y_i to its uniquely determined Boolean output. Thus exactly one y satisfies all gate equations, and it is C's evaluation tableau. Adding the output condition makes H_C satisfiable over y exactly when that tableau's output is 1. Each gate equation has constant-size Boolean implementation, and a binary AND tree combines the g equations and output condition using O(g) gates. This applies to one fixed deterministic circuit; it does not bound the cost of searching over candidate circuits for EXT or implement an EXT residual transition from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

Local gate constraints have constant-size implementations and their conjunction uses a linear-size binary AND tree.

label: S0826
statement:
statement: GATE-TRANSCRIPT PROJECTION LEMMA. Let C be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with m gates over AND, OR, and NOT, with primary input x and output wire o. Introduce one witness bit y_i for each gate output, in topological order. There is a fan-in-two circuit H_C(x,y) of O(m) gates that accepts exactly when every y_i equals the value of gate i on its predecessor wires and y_o=1. For every x there is exactly one gate-consistent transcript y, and C(x)=1 iff there exists y such that H_C(x,y)=1. Proof: For each gate i, a constant-size Boolean subcircuit checks equality between y_i and the AND, OR, or NOT of the at most two predecessor wires. A binary tree conjoins all consistency checks and the output bit, giving O(m) gates. Topological induction forces y_1, then y_2, and so on, uniquely to their gate values. The resulting transcript has y_o=C(x), so the conjunction is satisfiable exactly when C(x)=1.
proof: For each gate i construct a constant-size local equality check. Conjoin the m checks and output bit in a binary tree. Topological induction establishes uniqueness of the consistent transcript; its output wire equals C(x).

label: S0827
statement:
statement: FINITE-LANGUAGE PREFIX RESIDUAL COUNT LEMMA. Let L be a finite subset of {0,1}^N, and for each t in {0,...,N} and each p in {0,1}^t define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz is in L}. Then the number of distinct nonempty sets among {R_p: p in {0,1}^t} is at most min(2^t, |L|). If the empty set is counted as a residual, the number of distinct residuals is at most min(2^t, |L|)+1. Proof: There are 2^t prefixes, so at most 2^t distinct residuals of any kind. For each prefix p with R_p nonempty, choose one z_p in R_p. The map p -> pz_p is injective because its output has prefix p; hence the number of prefixes with nonempty residual is at most |L|. The number of distinct nonempty residual sets is no greater than the number of prefixes with nonempty residuals, proving the bound. The empty residual contributes at most one additional set. This lemma applies to L=Im(Eval_{n,s}) and bounds the canonical prefix automaton's distinct nonempty states at each fixed depth by min(2^t, |Im(Eval_{n,s})|); it does not bound transition circuit cost or give a polynomial bound in n,s.
derivation: Fix t. Let P_t={p in {0,1}^t:R_p is nonempty}. For each p in P_t, choose z_p with pz_p in L. If p≠q, then pz_p≠qz_q because their first t bits differ. Thus p↦pz_p is an injection P_t→L and |P_t|≤|L|. The number of distinct nonempty residuals is ≤|P_t|, and also ≤2^t. Adding the single possible empty residual yields the stated bound.

statement: LITERAL PREFIX-REGISTER UPDATE LEMMA (restricted model). For any Boolean relation H:{0,1}^N x {0,1}^r->{0,1}, store the observed prefix p in a register and retain H unchanged. On input bit b, update (p,H) to (pb,H). The represented residual after this update is exactly z' |-> exists w H(pb z',w). The update uses no Boolean gates only when register append/copy is the primitive transition operation; it stores t+1 prefix bits after t+1 inputs. This construction proves no transition-circuit bound when the next encoded state must be computed by a fan-in-two circuit.
derivation: Define R_p(z)=1 iff exists w H(pz,w). For every z', R_{pb}(z')=1 iff exists w H(pb z',w)=R_p(bz'), so the updated register represents the exact next residual. The state update itself appends b to p and leaves H unchanged. Under a register-write cost model this is a primitive update; under a Boolean-circuit cost model the register must be encoded and computed, so no zero-gate conclusion follows.

label: S0830
statement: statement: CANDIDATE-SET RESIDUAL LEMMA. Fix n,s and the standard fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit model with constants and wires free, and let F be the finite set of descriptions of circuits on n inputs with at most s gates (designated output included). For p∈{0,1}^t, define A_p={D∈F: Eval_D(x_i)=p_i for every i<t}, where x_0,…,x_{2^n−1} is the fixed truth-table input order. Then EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff A_p is nonempty, and A_{pb}={D∈A_p: Eval_D(x_t)=b}. If M=|F|, this state is represented by M bits and its update can be performed by testing each candidate circuit on x_t, in O(Ms) gate evaluations; M≤(s+1)(3(n+2s+2)^2)^s under a padded description encoding. Proof: by definition, D∈A_p exactly when its first t truth-table outputs equal p, so there exists a size-≤s circuit with prefix p iff A_p is nonempty. Appending b requires agreement on the first t positions and output b at position t, giving the displayed update equality in both directions. A circuit with j≤s ordered gates is described by at most 3 choices of gate type and at most (n+2s+2)^2 ordered source choices per gate, with at most s+1 choices for the designated output; summing j=0,…,s is bounded by the stated M. Testing one description on one input takes O(s) gate evaluations, so scanning the M-bit candidate vector costs O(Ms). This is an exact sufficient representation and update bound; it neither proves that the M-bit state is necessary nor provides a compact transition implementation.

structure.evidence: Direct finite-description construction and proof above; no computation is needed for this combinatorial bound. The result gives an explicit, generally exponential-in-s representation, not the O(s log(n+s))-bit EXT automaton state or a real-gate transition bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: statement: For any finite indexed family F=(f_1,...,f_M) of Boolean functions on {0,1}^N and prefix p of length t<N, define B_p={i: there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t} with f_i(pz)=1}. For b in {0,1}, define A_{p,b}={i: there exists z' in {0,1}^{N-t-1} with f_i(pb z')=1}. Then B_{pb}=B_p ∩ A_{p,b}. Therefore, given M-bit characteristic vectors for B_p and A_{p,b}, the update is coordinatewise AND and uses M two-input AND gates. This excludes the cost of constructing A_{p,b}. Proof: if i∈B_{pb}, a witnessing suffix z' yields suffix bz' for B_p, hence i∈B_p and i∈A_{p,b}. Conversely, i∈A_{p,b} has a suffix witnessing i∈B_{pb}; intersection with B_p does not remove it. Thus equality holds.

label: S0833
statement: statement: EXPLICIT CANDIDATE-SET TRANSITION CIRCUIT. Fix n,s, a finite circuit-description set F of size M, an input x_t, and a bit b. Let q_D indicate whether description D remains consistent with the prefix before x_t. The updated indicator is q'_D=q_D AND [Eval_D(x_t)=b] for every D∈F. There is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit computing q' from q with at most c M(s+1) gates for an absolute constant c, when each D has at most s gates and x_t is fixed; the circuit is constructible from (F,x_t,b) in O(Ms) time. Proof: For each D, unroll its at-most-s gate computation on the fixed input x_t into a Boolean circuit of at most c0(s+1) gates, obtaining the constant e_D=Eval_D(x_t). If e_D≠b, set q'_D=0 using a constant output; if e_D=b, wire q'_D directly to q_D. This already gives a circuit with no more than M wires and constants under the convention that constants and wiring are free. Under a stricter gate-only encoding with no free constants, use one shared constant generator and one AND gate per D to compute q_D AND [e_D=b], costing at most M+O(1) gates. Alternatively, if x_t is supplied as variable input rather than fixed, unroll each D's evaluation using at most c0(s+1) gates and compare its output to b and AND with q_D, using O(s+1) gates per D, hence at most cM(s+1). Correctness is coordinatewise: q'_D=1 exactly when q_D=1 and D outputs b on x_t, precisely the consistency condition after appending b. This is an explicit transition circuit for the candidate-set representation; its state dimension M may be exponential in s log(n+s), so it gives no compact-state result.

statement: statement: FIXED-POSITION RESIDUAL SEPARATION. Let L be any Boolean language on strings of a fixed length N, and for each t let R_p(z)=L(pz) for prefixes p of length t and suffixes z of length N-t. Let K_t be the number of distinct functions R_p. Every deterministic exact streaming algorithm deciding L must have at least K_t distinct internal configurations after t input bits; if configurations are encoded in fixed-length binary using b_t bits, then b_t >= ceil(log_2 K_t). Proof: Assume prefixes p,q of length t have the same configuration but R_p and R_q differ. Then there exists a suffix z with L(pz) != L(qz). Determinism and equality of the configurations imply that processing the common continuation z yields the same final answer from both prefixes, contradicting exactness. Thus each distinct residual function requires a distinct configuration. For L equal to the length-N prefix-extension language of EXT_{n,s}, this applies with R_p(z)=EXT_{n,s}(pz). This gives a necessary information bound only; it does not bound K_t or the real-gate cost of transitions.

statement: statement: EXPLICIT-FAMILY EXT RESIDUAL UPDATE LEMMA. Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be an explicitly listed family of pairwise distinct functions f_i:{0,1}^N->{0,1}, represented by their truth tables in a fixed coordinate order. For a prefix p of length t, define A_p={i : f_i[1..t]=p} and R_p={u in {0,1}^{N-t} : there exists i in A_p with f_i[t+1..N]=u}. For b in {0,1}, define A_{pb}={i in A_p : f_i[t+1]=b}. Then (i) A_{pb} is exactly the live-candidate set after reading b, (ii) R_{pb}={v : there exists i in A_{pb} with f_i[t+2..N]=v}, and (iii) the map i -> f_i[t+1..N] is injective on A_p. Given the explicit truth tables, A_{pb} is computed by scanning A_p and testing one bit per candidate, in O(M) time. Proof: By definitions, i belongs to A_{pb} iff f_i agrees with p and its next bit is b, exactly the condition that i survives the next prefix; the suffix set of those surviving candidates is the displayed R_{pb}. If i,j in A_p have the same remaining suffix, they also agree on the prefix p, so their full truth tables are equal, and pairwise distinctness implies i=j. A scan of at most M candidates performs one next-bit test per candidate and outputs exactly A_{pb}, taking O(M) time under an explicit-list representation. This is a finite-family representation/update lemma; it asserts no polynomial-in-s transition from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

label: S0839
statement: statement: Fix a Boolean circuit basis with q gate types of fan-in at most two, where constants and input wiring are free. Let H:{0,1}^N x {0,1}^r -> {0,1} have at most h gates, and define L(x)=1 iff there exists w in {0,1}^r with H(x,w)=1. For each fixed prefix length t, the number of distinct residual functions L_p(z)=L(pz), over p in {0,1}^t, is at most q^h (N+r+h+2)^(2h+1). Consequently the number over all prefix lengths is at most (N+1)q^h (N+r+h+2)^(2h+1). Proof: For each p, cofactor H by the constants in p; this yields a relation circuit on at most N remaining input bits and r witness bits using at most h gates. Its existential projection is L_p. Put K=N+r+h+2. An ordered description of an at-most-h-gate circuit chooses, at each of h gate positions, one of q types and at most K choices for each of two predecessor wires, then chooses one of at most K output wires. This gives at most (q K^2)^h K=q^h K^(2h+1) descriptions. Each description defines at most one relation and hence at most one projected residual, proving the bound. The count does not give an efficient canonicalization or transition algorithm.

structure.evidence: The proof is a direct count of ordered circuit descriptions in the stated fixed basis. Every projected residual at a fixed level has a cofactored witness-relation circuit of at most h gates; counting those circuits upper-bounds the number of projections.

statement: statement: Let A be any subset of {0,1}^N, and let D be a deterministic left-to-right machine deciding A. For each prefix p of length t define A_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz is in A}. At level t, D must have at least as many states as there are distinct residuals A_p. Proof: if two prefixes p,p' leave D in the same state, then for every suffix z the continuation from that state is identical, so pz is accepted iff p'z is accepted. Thus A_p=A_p'. Therefore prefixes with distinct residuals occupy distinct states.

structure.evidence: The same-state implication follows directly from determinism and the fact that the remaining suffix is identical. This formalizes the state-count lower bound for fixed-length streaming recognition; it does not bound update time or relate an arbitrary MCSP decider to EXT.

statement: statement: DISTINCT-WITNESS-COFACTOR ELIMINATION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} have a fan-in-two circuit of h gates. Let d be the number of distinct Boolean functions f_w(x)=H(x,w), for w∈{0,1}^r. Then G(x)=∃w H(x,w) has a fan-in-two circuit of at most d(h+1)-1 gates. For every prefix p, G_p(z)=G(pz) has a circuit of no greater size, and its next cofactor G_{pb} is obtained by input substitution without increasing size. Proof: Choose one representative witness w_j from each of the d equivalence classes under f_w=f_{w'}. For each representative, substitute w_j into a copy of H, obtaining f_{w_j} with at most h gates. OR the d outputs with a binary tree using d−1 gates. For each x, this OR is 1 iff at least one representative class has H(x,w_j)=1; since each class has identical f_w, this is equivalent to ∃w H(x,w)=1. Thus the size is at most dh+d−1=d(h+1)−1. Fixing prefix coordinates in the resulting circuit cannot increase the number of gates, proving the cofactor statements. This can improve the 2^r witness-enumeration bound when d<2^r; it supplies no general bound on d and no transition-cost lower bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0846
statement: statement: PREFIXWISE DISTINCT-COFACTOR PROJECTION BOUND. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} have a fan-in-two circuit with h gates. For a prefix p of length t, let F_p be the set of distinct Boolean functions z↦H(pz,w), over w∈{0,1}^r, and d_p=|F_p|. Then the projected residual L_p(z)=∨_{w}H(pz,w) is computed by a fan-in-two circuit with at most d_p(h+1)−1 gates. After reading bit b, every member of F_{pb} is obtained by cofactoring some member of F_p at its first suffix input; therefore d_{pb}≤d_p, and this representation can be updated by cofactoring each retained function and removing duplicates. Proof: For each f∈F_p, take one circuit computing f and OR the d_p outputs using d_p−1 gates. Repeated witness functions do not change this OR, proving the size bound. For any suffix z', L_{pb}(z')=∨_w H(pb z',w)=∨_w H(p(bz'),w)=L_p(bz'). Also each function z'↦H(pb z',w) is the cofactor at b of z↦H(pz,w), so the distinct set at pb is a subset of the cofactored images of F_p and has size at most d_p. This is a representation-size bound only: identifying equal cofactors may require expensive computation, and the bound does not give a compact update algorithm for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement:
statement: For fixed n,s, let F_{n,s} be the length-N truth tables computed by circuits of size at most s. For every prefix p let R_p={z:pz in F_{n,s}}. The minimum number of states of a deterministic automaton recognizing the prefix language of F_{n,s} is D=|{R_p:p a prefix}|; consequently any exact state encoding requires at least ceil(log2 D) bits.
proof: If R_p=R_q, every suffix is accepted after p iff it is accepted after q, so merging them preserves the language. If R_p differs from R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference; then exactly one of pz,qz belongs to F_{n,s}, so merging p,q misclassifies one. Therefore equality of completion sets is precisely the indistinguishability equivalence, and its D classes are necessary and sufficient states. D distinct states require at least ceil(log2 D) bits.

label: S0849
statement: For a finite family F⊆{0,1}^N, define R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N−|p|}: pz∈F} for every binary prefix p of length at most N. The minimum number of states in a deterministic automaton that recognizes exactly the prefixes of words in F is the number D of distinct sets R_p, including the empty set when it occurs. Proof: Each prefix p has residual language R_p. If R_p=R_q, then for each next bit b and each remaining suffix z, bz∈R_p iff bz∈R_q, so p and q have identical acceptance behavior for every continuation and may be merged. Conversely, if R_p≠R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference; the continuation z is accepted from exactly one of p,q, so any deterministic automaton recognizing the language must place them in different states. Thus the equivalence classes of prefixes under equality of residual languages are exactly the necessary and sufficient states, and their number is D.

statement: PREFIX-CLOSURE RESIDUAL CHARACTERIZATION. Let N≥0, F⊆{0,1}^N, P=Pref(F), and for p∈P let R_p={u∈{0,1}^{N−|p|}: pu∈F}. Let K_p={z∈{0,1}^{≤N−|p|}: pz∈P}. Then K_p=Pref(R_p): z∈K_p iff z is a prefix of some u∈R_p. Consequently K_p=K_q iff either |p|=|q| and R_p=R_q, or R_p=R_q=∅.
proof: For z of length at most N−|p|, pz∈P iff there exists y with pzy∈F, by prefix closure. This is equivalent to zy∈R_p for some y, meaning z is a prefix of an element of R_p. If R_p and R_q are nonempty at different depths, their words have different fixed lengths, so their prefix languages have different maximum word lengths. At equal depth, equality of R sets implies equality of prefix sets; conversely, elements of R_p have maximum remaining length and so are exactly the maximum-length elements of Pref(R_p), recovering R_p from that prefix language. Empty residuals yield the same empty continuation language at every depth. Myhill–Nerode then says precisely the equal continuation languages can be merged, while unequal ones are distinguished by a continuation in their symmetric difference.

label: S0851
statement: WIRE-CONSISTENCY REPRESENTATION. Let C be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with g gates, topologically ordered, and output wire o. Introduce one bit w_i for each gate. Let H_C(y,w) assert, for every i, that w_i equals gate i applied to its input wires, and also assert o=1. Then H_C has O(g) fan-in-two gates, and C(y)=1 iff there exists w with H_C(y,w)=1. For every y, the gate equations force a unique w. Proof: Induct in topological order: each gate’s inputs are primary inputs or earlier gate outputs, so its equation uniquely sets w_i to the value computed by C. Thus the unique satisfying assignment to the gate equations is C’s evaluation; adding o=1 makes the existential projection accept exactly when C(y)=1. Each local equation has constant-size implementation and their conjunction uses O(g) gates. This representation does not bound the cost of updating or canonicalizing projected residuals.

statement: MINIMAL EXACT RECOGNIZER STATES ARE RESIDUAL LANGUAGES. Let L be a language over a finite alphabet and let P be the set of prefixes under consideration. For p define R_p={z:pz∈L}. Every deterministic exact recognizer has distinct states after p and q whenever R_p≠R_q; conversely, the distinct residuals form the states of an exact recognizer, with transition R_p --a--> R_{pa} and acceptance iff the empty suffix belongs to the residual. Thus the minimum number of states reachable by prefixes in P is exactly the number of distinct residuals among P. Proof: If R_p≠R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference. A recognizer in the same state after p and q processes z identically, contradicting exactness. For the converse, define the transition by R_p→R_{pa}; it is well-defined because R_p=R_q implies for every a,z, az∈R_p iff az∈R_q, hence R_{pa}=R_{qa}. Also R_p is accepting exactly when ε∈R_p, which is equivalent to p∈L. This characterizes precisely the information any exact prefix recognizer must retain. It gives no lower bound on real-gate transition cost for H_C and no implication for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

Proof: define L_p(z)=∃w H(pz,w). Then L_pb(z')=1 iff ∃w H(pb z',w)=1 iff L_p(bz')=1. The update appends b to p; H is untouched, so gate count remains h. This gives an exact construction and update-cost bound in representation (H,p), while explicitly charging |p| bits and making no compactness or canonicality claim.

statement: statement_start: DISTINGUISHING-SUFFIX SIGNATURE LEMMA. Let U be a finite suffix set and let R_1,...,R_K be distinct subsets of U. For every unordered pair {i,j}, choose u_{ij} in the symmetric difference R_i triangle R_j. Define sigma(R_i) as its membership vector over the chosen suffixes. Then sigma is injective and uses at most binomial(K,2) coordinates. Conversely, any injective binary signature for these K residuals requires at least ceil(log_2 K) coordinates. Proof: For i != j, the selected u_{ij} belongs to exactly one of R_i,R_j, so their corresponding coordinate differs and sigma(R_i) != sigma(R_j). There are binomial(K,2) pairs, hence no more than that many chosen coordinates (duplicates can be removed). A q-coordinate binary vector has at most 2^q possible values, so injectivity implies K <= 2^q and q >= ceil(log_2 K). For K=0 or 1, the empty coordinate set is injective and the lower bound is zero. At an EXT prefix level, take U to be the set of all suffixes of the remaining length and the R_i to be its distinct residual languages; the same result applies exactly. This gives a finite separating feature set once the witnesses are selected, but does not construct the witnesses efficiently or bound update cost from H_C.

statement: statement_start: FINITE-FAMILY PREFIX RESIDUAL BOUND. For F subset {0,1}^N with |F|=M and 0<=t<=N, the number K_t of distinct residual sets F_p={z:pz in F}, p in {0,1}^t, is at most min(2^t,M)+1. Proof: there are 2^t prefixes. Every nonempty residual comes from an extendable prefix. Distinct extendable prefixes each contain a distinct member of F, so there are at most M such prefixes and at most M nonempty residuals. There is at most one additional empty residual. Thus K_t<=min(2^t,M)+1. The levelwise minimal deterministic residual automaton has at most sum_{t=0}^N (min(2^t,M)+1) states. The update after bit b is exactly F_{pb}={z:bz in F_p}, by definition. This finite-family bound does not bound real-gate transition cost for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits or improve the known EXT bound when M is large.

statement: statement_start: EXT DESCRIPTION-COUNT RESIDUAL BOUND. Fix n,s and a finite encoding of fan-in-two Boolean circuits of size at most s, with at most B distinct descriptions. Let F be the set of their N-bit truth tables, N=2^n. At every prefix length t, the number of distinct residual sets F_p={z:pz in F} is at most min(2^t,|F|)+1, hence at most B+1. Proof: There are 2^t prefixes. Every nonempty residual belongs to an extendable prefix; distinct extendable prefixes contain disjoint sets of full truth tables, so choosing one table from each gives at most |F| such prefixes. There is at most one empty residual. Also |F|<=B because each description computes one table. Thus the bound follows. Encoding each residual by its prefix-history trie state takes at most ceil(log2(B+1)) bits at a level, and its exact transition is residual R -> {z:bz in R}. This bounds the states needed for EXT from description count; it does not give bounded real-gate transitions for an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

label: S0858
statement:
statement: Residual-trie construction. For any finite A subset {0,1}^N, let R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pz in A}. At each depth t, use one state for each distinct nonempty R_p with |p|=t, plus a dead state. From state R_p on bit b, transition to R_{pb} if nonempty, otherwise dead; dead loops to itself. Accept at depth N exactly when the residual contains the empty string. This deterministic automaton recognizes A and has at most 1+sum_{t=0}^N D_t states, where D_t is the number of distinct nonempty residuals at depth t.
proof: For every prefix p represented by R_p, its continuation z is accepted exactly when z is in R_p, by definition. After reading b then suffix z, acceptance is equivalent to bz in R_p, which is equivalent to z in R_{pb}; if R_{pb} is empty no completion is in A and the dead state is correct. Distinct prefixes with the same residual therefore have identical future behavior, so identifying them is safe. At depth N, the only possible residual is {epsilon} for words in A, and the empty residual is represented by dead. Thus the stated state count and language recognition follow.

statement:
statement: Explicit candidate-set transition for EXT. Fix n and s, and let C be the finite set of fan-in-two circuit descriptions of size at most s over a fixed finite gate basis, with fixed encodings of inputs and output. For each prefix p of length t define S_p={D in C: Eval(D) has prefix p}. Then the residual EXT_{n,s}|p is nonempty exactly when S_p is nonempty. On reading bit b, S_{pb}={D in S_p: Eval(D)_{t+1}=b}. This representation admits an update circuit with O(M(n,s)(s+log(n+s))) fan-in-two gates, where M(n,s)=|C|, when the truth-table index is supplied in binary. This is an upper bound for this representation, not a lower bound or a transition bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
proof: For each D in C, evaluate its output on the input indexed by t+1. Its at-most-s gates can be evaluated using O(s) gates; decoding the binary index costs O(log(n+s)) under the stated model. Compare the output with b and AND that match bit with D's old membership bit in S_p. Parallelizing over M descriptions produces the membership vector for S_{pb} using O(M(s+log(n+s))) gates. A suffix z completes p to a word in Im(Eval) exactly when some D in S_p agrees with all bits of z, so S_p represents the residual exactly. Filtering by the next bit therefore gives the exact next candidate set and the stated cost.

statement:
statement: Fixed-position candidate-set update lemma. Fix n,s, a finite encoded family C of M Boolean circuits D:{0,1}^n->{0,1} of size at most s, and an ordering x_0,...,x_{2^n-1} of their truth-table inputs. For a length-t prefix p define u_p(D)=1 exactly when D(x_j)=p_j for every j<t. At level t, reading bit b updates the membership vector by u_{pb}(D)=u_p(D) AND [D(x_t)=b]. With the position t fixed by the level, this update is implementable by a fan-in-two circuit of at most M AND gates, with the constants [D(x_t)=b] hardwired. The representation uses M state bits. It is exact for EXT_{n,s}, but this bound is for the explicit candidate-set representation and makes no claim about compact state or transitions for an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.
proof: By definition, D belongs to the candidate set after pb iff it agrees with p on all positions j<t and agrees with b at position t. The first condition is u_p(D)=1 and the second is the fixed Boolean constant [D(x_t)=b]. Their conjunction gives the displayed update independently for every D. Thus the updated vector represents exactly the circuits whose truth tables extend pb. A suffix completes pb to a truth table in the family iff at least one such circuit agrees with every remaining bit, so the represented candidate set determines the EXT residual exactly. Each output coordinate requires at most one AND gate when constants and wiring are free, giving at most M gates total.

label: S0861
statement:
statement: Candidate-set residual-count lemma. Fix n,s and a finite family C of M Boolean circuits D:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, with truth-table input order x_0,...,x_{2^n-1}. For each prefix p, let S_p={D in C: D agrees with p on its positions}. The number of distinct residual languages EXT_{n,s}|p, over all prefixes p at all levels, is at most 2^M. In particular, at any fixed level t it is at most min(2^t,2^M).
proof: For each prefix p define its residual R_p={z: there exists D in S_p whose outputs on the positions after p equal z}. Thus R_p is determined entirely by S_p: if S_p=S_q, then the same circuits remain and have the same remaining truth-table outputs, so R_p=R_q. There are at most 2^M subsets of C, hence at most 2^M distinct residual languages across all prefixes. At level t there are 2^t prefixes, giving the additional bound 2^t. This proves the claim. The bound is a representation-specific upper bound; it gives no lower bound on the number of states needed by other representations and no transition bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: statement: FIXED-BIT RESIDUAL OR-TRANSITION LEMMA. Let F be a nonempty finite subset of {0,1}^N and 0<=t<N. Let S_t be its distinct prefix residuals at level t, augmented by the empty set, and let d=|S_t|. For each fixed bit b, map R to T_b(R)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R}. The one-hot transition on valid states is computed by OR-ing source coordinates in each destination fiber, with at most d-1 fan-in-two OR gates. Proof: For every source residual R, T_b(R) is a next-level residual, and the empty residual maps to itself. Thus the source states partition into nonempty fibers B_T={R:T_b(R)=T}. Define output y_T=OR_{R in B_T} x_R, using |B_T|-1 gates per fiber. On valid one-hot input e_R0, exactly y_{T_b(R0)} is 1. If q fibers are nonempty, total gates are sum_T(|B_T|-1)=d-q<=d-1. This is a separate circuit for fixed b, under a valid one-hot promise; it does not claim a joint circuit taking b as input or a polynomial bound on d for EXT.

label: S0865
statement:
statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITION BOUND. Let L be a language of binary strings of fixed length N. At depth t, let R_t be the set of distinct residual languages L_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}, over prefixes p of length t, and put r_t=|R_t|. For each residual R in R_t and bit b, its child is R_b={z: bz in R}, which lies in R_{t+1}. Encode a residual by its one-hot vector over R_t. The deterministic update on input b from layer t to t+1 has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most r_t-1 OR gates (besides free wires/constants), producing the one-hot child vector.
proof: For each Q in R_{t+1}, define its fiber F_Q={R in R_t: R_b=Q}. The output coordinate for Q is the OR of the input coordinates indexed by F_Q; this is exact because the input is one-hot and each residual has exactly one child. A fiber of size k>0 needs k-1 binary OR gates, and an empty fiber needs zero gates (constant 0). The nonempty fibers partition R_t, so summing their costs gives r_t-|im(child)|≤r_t-1, since R_t is nonempty and hence the image has at least one element. This constructs the update circuit and proves the bound.

statement: statement: BLOCK-CONTROLLED RESIDUAL TRANSITION LEMMA. Let L be a language of fixed-length binary strings, and at depth t let R_t be its r distinct residuals. For a block length k with t+k<=N, each block a in {0,1}^k induces a deterministic map f_a:R_t -> R_{t+k}, where f_a(R)={z: az in R}. If the block a is supplied as an external control (not computed by the transition circuit), then the one-hot encoding of R is updated exactly to the one-hot encoding of f_a(R) using at most r-1 fan-in-two OR gates. Proof: For each Q in R_{t+k}, let F_Q={R in R_t:f_a(R)=Q}. Output coordinate Q is the OR of input coordinates in F_Q (or constant 0 if empty). Since the input is one-hot, exactly the coordinate for f_a(R) is set. A fiber of size q costs max(q-1,0) OR gates. Nonempty fibers partition R_t, so total cost is r-|im(f_a)|<=r-1, since R_t is nonempty. This only bounds the controlled update; it does not include computing a or provide a compact canonical encoding.

statement: statement: INPUT-CHARGED ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITION. Let R and R' be nonempty finite sets, |R|=r, and let f_0,f_1:R→R' be arbitrary maps. In the circuit model with fan-in-two AND/OR and NOT gates all charged, a circuit taking a one-hot encoding x of an element of R and a bit b outputs the one-hot encoding of f_b(x) using at most 4r gates on valid one-hot inputs. Proof: Compute ¬b once. For each i∈R compute u_i=x_i∧b and v_i=x_i∧¬b, using 2r gates. For each j∈R', output y_j as the OR of all u_i with f_1(i)=j and all v_i with f_0(i)=j; an empty OR is constant 0. Across all outputs these term lists partition the 2r terms, so binary OR trees use at most 2r−1 gates. Total is 1+2r+(2r−1)=4r. For a valid one-hot x, exactly the term selected by b and its unique source coordinate is 1, and it appears at output f_b(i); hence outputs are exactly one-hot. This repairs the transition-cost statement with an explicit input convention and charged NOT gate. It concerns arbitrary finite transition maps and does not provide a compact encoding or a transition procedure for H_C / EXT.

statement: statement: RESIDUAL DISTINGUISHABILITY LOWER BOUND. Let L be any language of fixed-length strings {0,1}^N. For each t in {0,...,N}, let R_t={L_p:p in {0,1}^t}, where L_p(z)=1 iff pz is in L. Any deterministic one-pass streaming machine that, after reading each length-t prefix, stores a state from which it can correctly decide membership for every continuation z of length N-t must have at least |R_t| distinct states at level t. Proof: Suppose two prefixes p,q of length t with L_p != L_q led to the same state. Since the residual functions differ, there exists a suffix z of length N-t for which exactly one of pz,qz belongs to L. Starting from the same state and then reading the same z forces a deterministic machine to produce the same final answer on both strings, contradicting correctness. Thus prefixes with distinct residuals must occupy distinct states, giving at least |R_t| states. In particular the state requires at least ceil(log2 |R_t|) bits. For EXT_{n,s}, this applies to the exact prefix language over truth-table strings, but by itself neither bounds |R_t| superpolynomially for the relevant threshold nor charges the cost of deriving transitions from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

Starting from the same state and then reading the same z forces a deterministic machine to produce the same final answer on both strings, contradicting correctness. Thus prefixes with distinct residuals must occupy distinct states, giving at least |R_t| states. In particular the state requires at least ceil(log2 |R_t|) bits. For EXT_{n,s}, this applies to the exact prefix language over truth-table strings, but by itself neither bounds |R_t| superpolynomially for the relevant threshold nor charges the cost of deriving transitions from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

statement: RESIDUAL-TABLE TRANSITION LEMMA. For L⊆{0,1}^N and prefix p, let T_p be the lexicographically ordered truth table of z↦1[pz∈L]. If a level has D distinct residual functions, any deterministic exact state encoding with a decoder needs at least log₂D bits.

label: S0870
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL COUNTING LEMMA. Fix a finite Boolean gate basis of size g and a standard fan-in-two circuit model with N input bits and h gates. Let D_t be the number of distinct residual functions L_p(z)=L(pz) over prefixes p of length t, where L is computed by such a circuit. Then D_t ≤ min(2^t, (g(N+h+2)^2)^h (N+h+1)) for h≥1; for h=0, D_t≤min(2^t,N+1).
proof: There are 2^t prefixes, so D_t≤2^t. Each residual is computed by the original circuit after fixing t input wires, hence by a circuit with at most h gates and at most N remaining inputs. To count descriptions, order the gates topologically. For each gate choose one of g types and two incoming wires from at most N+h+2 available inputs or earlier gates; choose one output wire from at most N+h+1 wires. Thus the number of descriptions is at most (g(N+h+2)^2)^h(N+h+1), which bounds the number of functions represented. If h=0, the output is an input or a constant, giving at most N+1 functions. Combining the two bounds proves the claim.

statement:
statement: WITNESS-ELIMINATION CIRCUIT BOUND. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates. Then G(x)=1 iff there exists w∈{0,1}^r with H(x,w)=1 has a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^r(h+1)-1 gates. For every prefix p of x, the cofactor G_p has a circuit with no more than this bound.
proof: For each w∈{0,1}^r, copy the h-gate circuit H and substitute the constants of w on its witness inputs. The resulting circuit computes x↦H(x,w) and uses at most h gates. OR the 2^r outputs with a binary tree, which uses 2^r−1 gates. The total is at most 2^r h +(2^r−1)=2^r(h+1)−1, and this computes G by existential semantics. Fixing the coordinates of any prefix p by input substitution cannot increase the gate count, giving the same bound for G_p.

statement:
statement: DISTINCT-WITNESS-SLICE ELIMINATION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two circuit with h gates. For each w define H_w(x)=H(x,w), and let q be the number of distinct Boolean functions among {H_w : w∈{0,1}^r}. Then G(x)=1 iff ∃w H(x,w)=1 has a fan-in-two circuit with at most q(h+1)-1 gates. Every prefix cofactor of G has a circuit within the same bound.
proof: Choose one representative witness w_i for each of the q distinct functions H_w. For each representative, copy H and substitute the constants w_i on its witness inputs; this computes H_{w_i} with at most h gates. OR the q outputs with a binary tree of q−1 OR gates. The resulting circuit computes G, since duplicate slices do not change an OR and every witness assignment belongs to one represented slice. Its size is at most qh+(q−1)=q(h+1)-1. Fixing the input coordinates of any prefix cofactor cannot increase circuit size, so the same bound holds for every prefix.

label: S0873
statement:
statement: COFACTOR MONOTONICITY OF DISTINCT WITNESS SLICES. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1}. For a prefix p of length t, let q_p be the number of distinct functions z↦H(pz,w), as w ranges over {0,1}^r. For every next bit b, q_{pb}≤q_p. Consequently, if H has a fan-in-two circuit with h gates, the existential projection G_p(z)=∃w H(pz,w) has a fan-in-two circuit of at most q_p(h+1)-1 gates at every prefix, and this bound never increases along a path.
proof: For each witness w, write f_w(z)=H(pz,w). Its child slice is f_{w,b}(z')=H(pbz',w)=f_w(bz'), the cofactor of f_w obtained by fixing its first input to b. If f_w=f_{w'} as functions on all suffixes z, then f_w(bz')=f_{w'}(bz') for every z'; hence the map from parent slice classes to child slice classes is well-defined and surjective onto the set of child classes. Therefore q_{pb}≤q_p. Applying the distinct-slice elimination construction to the child relation yields a circuit for G_{pb} of size at most q_{pb}(h+1)-1, which is no larger than q_p(h+1)-1. The same argument applies at every prefix, including the empty and full prefixes.

label: S0877
statement: PACKED EXPLICIT TRANSITION TABLE LEMMA. Let D={0,1}^k be a set of d=2^k state codes and let T:D×{0,1}→D be any fixed transition table. There is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O(dk) gates computing T(q,b) on every q∈D and b∈{0,1}. Proof: For each u∈D form selector e_u=[q=u], using k input literals and a binary AND tree, with at most O(k) gates per u. For output coordinate j, form the OR of e_u AND [T(u,b)_j=1] over all (u,b) pairs, additionally selecting the corresponding input bit b; equivalently use selectors [q=u] AND [b=β] for each pair (u,β). There are 2d selectors, each costing O(k), and at most 2dk selector-to-output incidences, whose OR trees cost O(dk) total. The output bits therefore equal T(q,b) for every valid code q. Padding unused codes with arbitrary transitions gives a total circuit. The bound concerns a known nonuniform table and does not include the cost of constructing that table or converting an EXT state from an H_C representation.

label: S0878
statement: FINITE-IMAGE RESIDUAL COUNT LEMMA. Let F be a finite subset of {0,1}^N with |F|=M. For each t in {0,...,N} and p in {0,1}^t, define R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}. At each level t there are at most M+1 distinct residuals, and across all levels there are at most (N+1)(M+1) level-tagged residual states. Proof: Fix t. Every nonempty residual R_t(p) has a witness z with pz in F. For distinct prefixes p,p' of length t, the sets of strings extending them are disjoint. Choose one prefix and one witness for each distinct nonempty residual. These witnesses are distinct: if two chosen witnesses were the same string, its length-t prefix would determine the same prefix and hence the same residual. Thus there are at most M nonempty residuals. The empty residual contributes at most one more. Summing over the N+1 levels gives at most (N+1)(M+1) level-tagged states. They can be assigned binary labels of length ceil(log2((N+1)(M+1))). This is only a state-count and encoding bound; it gives no efficient way to compute labels or transitions from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

label: S0879
statement:
statement: EXPLICIT-CANDIDATE FILTER UPDATE LEMMA. For every N,M≥0 and every explicitly listed family F=(f_1,...,f_M)⊆{0,1}^N, define a prefix-agreement state a∈{0,1}^M at level t by a_j=1 iff f_j[0:t]=p. For each t<N and next bit b, the coordinate update a'_j=a_j AND [f_j(t)=b] produces exactly the agreement state for pb and is computable by a nonuniform fan-in-two circuit of at most M+1 gates. The lemma holds for empty families and all prefixes, including t=0 and t=N−1.
proof: For each j, a'_j=1 iff a_j=1 and f_j(t)=b. By the definition of a_j, this is equivalent to f_j[0:t]=p and f_j(t)=b, which is equivalent to f_j[0:t+1]=pb. Thus the output vector is exactly the prefix-agreement vector at level t+1. At a fixed level the bits f_j(t) are constants. If the constant is 1, the coordinate is a_j AND b; if it is 0, it is a_j AND NOT b. Share one NOT b gate across all coordinates, and use one AND gate per coordinate, for at most M+1 gates. For M=0 no coordinate gates are needed. At t=N−1 the resulting vector marks exactly the listed words equal to the full word pb. This proof makes no claim about compressing the M-bit state or computing it from an arbitrary decision circuit H_C.

structure.lemma: Explicit-candidate residual update lemma: Let F=(f_1,...,f_M) be an explicitly listed family of Boolean words of common length N. At level t, store a∈{0,1}^M with a_j=1 exactly when f_j[0:t]=p. On reading b, update a_j' = a_j AND [f_j(t)=b]. This update is computable in at most M+1 fan-in-two gates and produces exactly the state for pb. Proof: for every j, a_j'=1 iff f_j[0:t]=p and f_j(t)=b, iff f_j[0:t+1]=pb. At a fixed level, f_j(t) is a constant. Use a_j AND b when it is 1, and a_j AND NOT b when it is 0, sharing one NOT gate. Thus at most M+1 gates; M=0 is immediate. The state uses M bits and constants require the explicit list. No bound follows for exponentially many candidate circuits or for conversion from arbitrary H_C.

statement: EXPLICIT-LIST AGREEMENT UPDATE LEMMA. Let F=(f_1,...,f_M) be a listed family of distinct bit strings of length N. At level t encode prefix p by a_j=1 iff f_j begins with p. On reading b, set a'_j=a_j AND [f_j(t)=b]. This is exact and costs at most M fan-in-two gates, since each [f_j(t)=b] is a level-specific constant. The vector identifies the listed strings compatible with p and hence their suffix set. Proof: For every j, a'_j=1 iff f_j begins with p and its next bit equals b, iff f_j begins with pb. Therefore the updated vector is exactly the agreement vector for pb. Each coordinate is a constant, wire, or one AND gate. This applies only to an explicit listed family and gives no polynomial-in-s transition bound for succinct circuit families or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: EXPLICIT-EXT UPDATE BOUND. Fix n,s and an explicit list F of all distinct truth tables computed by fan-in-two Boolean circuits with n inputs and at most s gates, under any fixed circuit encoding. Let M=|F|. The prefix survivor-vector transition for EXT_{n,s} is exact and uses at most M fan-in-two gates per input bit. Proof: Index the tables f_1,...,f_M. At level t store a_j=1 iff f_j agrees with the current prefix on its first t positions. On reading bit b, set a'_j=a_j AND [f_j(t)=b]. The bracket is a level-specific constant, so each coordinate needs at most one AND gate. Thus a' records exactly the tables agreeing with the extended prefix. Initially all coordinates are 1, and induction proves the invariant at every level. This is a nonuniform explicit-list construction; its transition bound is M and does not imply poly(s,n) cost because the list may be exponentially large in s log(n+s).

statement:
statement: For F={0,1}^N, the survivor vectors of distinct length-t prefixes are pairwise distinct; hence any injective binary encoding of all reachable survivor states at level t requires at least t bits.
derivation: For a prefix p, let a_p(x)=1 iff x begins with p, for each x in F. If p and q are distinct length-t strings, choose any x extending p; then a_p(x)=1 and a_q(x)=0. Thus p↦a_p is injective on the 2^t prefixes. An injective encoding of 2^t states by B bits requires 2^B≥2^t, so B≥t.

statement: statement: EXPLICIT-FAMILY PREFIX UPDATE (independent proof attempt). Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be an explicitly listed family of binary strings of common length N. After prefix p, store a_j=1 iff f_j begins with p. On reading bit b, define a'_j=a_j if the (|p|+1)-st bit of f_j equals b, and a'_j=0 otherwise. Then a' encodes exactly the members of F beginning with pb. Proof: For each j, a'_j=1 iff a_j=1 and f_j[|p|+1]=b, which holds iff f_j begins with p and has next bit b, equivalently iff f_j begins with pb. Each output is a wire from a_j or constant zero, so the Boolean gate cost is zero when wiring/constants are free. All transitions can be constructed by scanning the explicit family in O(MN) time. This gives no polynomial bound for implicit circuit families.

statement: statement: EXPLICIT-FAMILY BINARY RESIDUAL AUTOMATON. Let F be an explicitly listed set of M distinct strings in {0,1}^N. For each level t, define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. There are at most M+1 distinct residuals at level t: the empty set and at most M nonempty residuals. Indeed, if two nonempty residuals R_t(p),R_t(p') intersect, some f in F has both p and p' as its length-t prefix, hence p=p' and the residuals are equal. Index the distinct residuals at each level by 0,...,d_t-1, where d_t<=M+1, and encode an index in k=ceil(log2(M+1)) bits (with the trivial M=0 case handled by one state). For each level, the transition function on a valid state index and input bit b is a Boolean function on at most 2(M+1) input pairs, with output the index of the b-section {u:bu in R}; such a section is exactly the next-level residual reached by appending b. Extend the function arbitrarily to invalid codes. A multiplexer tree over the k+1 input bits computes each output bit with O(2^(k+1))=O(M+1) fan-in-two gates, so the transition circuit uses O((M+1)log(M+1)) gates. Given the explicit list, all level residual indices and transition tables are constructible by scanning the strings and their prefixes. This is an exact construction for explicit F only; since M may be exponential in the circuit-size parameter for the implicit family of small circuits, it gives no poly(s) transition bound and does not close G0004.

Index the distinct residuals at each level by 0,...,d_t-1, where d_t<=M+1, and encode an index in k=ceil(log2(M+1)) bits (with the trivial M=0 case handled by one state). For each level, the transition function on a valid state index and input bit b is a Boolean function on at most 2(M+1) input pairs, with output the index of the b-section {u:bu in R}; such a section is exactly the next-level residual reached by appending b. Extend the function arbitrarily to invalid codes. A multiplexer tree over the k+1 input bits computes each output bit with O(2^(k+1))=O(M+1) fan-in-two gates, so the transition circuit uses O((M+1)log(M+1)) gates. Given the explicit list, all level residual indices and transition tables are constructible by scanning the strings and their prefixes. This is an exact construction for explicit F only; since M may be exponential in the circuit-size parameter for the implicit family of small circuits, it gives no poly(s) transition bound and does not close G0004.

statement: statement: SHARED TSEITIN ENCODING FOR ALL EXT PREFIX QUERIES. Let C be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with N input bits and s gates, and introduce one variable y_g for each gate g. There is a CNF formula T_C(x,y) with O(s) clauses and O(s) variables such that, for every input x, C(x)=1 iff there exists y satisfying T_C(x,y) together with the unit clause requiring the output gate to be 1. For each prefix p of length t<N and bit b, EXT_C(pb)=1 iff the same T_C, together with output=1 and the t+1 unit assumptions x_1=p_1,...,x_t=p_t,x_{t+1}=b, is satisfiable. Thus one encoding of C is shared across all prefix transitions; each transition changes only the prefix assumptions, adding one unit assumption. Proof: For each gate, encode its Boolean truth-table relation between its input wires and output wire by a constant number of clauses; conjoin these clauses over all gates and require the output wire to be 1. Given x, the circuit's unique gate evaluation supplies a satisfying y exactly when C(x)=1, and any satisfying y must agree with that evaluation gate by gate in topological order. For a fixed prefix, the remaining input variables are existentially free, so satisfiability of the stated CNF under the prefix units is equivalent to the existence of an accepting completion. The construction uses O(s) clauses and variables and is independent of the chosen prefix. This yields a shared existential-CNF representation of EXT transitions, but does not give a deterministic bounded-gate transition circuit after eliminating the free input and gate variables, nor a reduction to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement:
statement_start: EXPLICIT-CANDIDATE MASK TRANSITION TRADEOFF. Fix n,s and a finite, explicitly indexed family C of Boolean circuits on N-bit truth-table inputs, with M=|C|. For each prefix p of length t, store vector q_p in {0,1}^M whose coordinate C is 1 iff C's truth table begins with p. For next bit b, q_{pb}(C)=q_p(C) AND [the (t+1)st truth-table bit of C equals b]. For fixed t,b,C the bracket is a hardwired constant, so each output is either its corresponding input bit or constant 0: the transition is exact and uses zero Boolean gates, with M state bits and O(M) output wires/constants. EXT(p) is exactly OR_C q_p(C), decidable with at most M-1 fan-in-two gates. Proof: By definition q_{pb}(C)=1 exactly when C matches p and its next truth-table bit equals b, precisely when C matches pb. This proves the coordinatewise update. The OR is 1 exactly when at least one candidate circuit extends p, the definition of EXT. This result applies to any fixed finite explicit candidate family; it makes no polynomial-workspace claim.

statement:
statement: SURVIVOR-MASK EXTENSION LEMMA. Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be a finite indexed family of Boolean strings of length N, with each f_j explicitly available. At prefix length t, let A(p)={j:f_j[1..t]=p}. The mask m(p) in {0,1}^M whose jth bit is 1 iff j is in A(p) is an exact representation of EXT_F(p): EXT_F(p)=1 iff |A(p)|>0. Given m(p) and next bit b, the mask m(pb) is computed by M fan-in-two gates, one per index, since m'_j=m_j AND [f_j[t+1]=b], where bracket is a hardwired constant. For all prefixes and all t<N, induction gives the invariant that m(p) marks exactly the family members extending p. Consequently, after preprocessing the explicit family, the entire EXT_F automaton has a deterministic transition circuit of size M at each level and uses M state bits; preprocessing time is O(MN). Proof: At t=0 all indices extend the empty prefix. Assuming the invariant at p, index j extends pb iff it extends p and its (t+1)st bit equals b. This is precisely the displayed update. Induction proves exactness. The output bit is the OR of the M mask bits, so acceptance is also computable in at most M-1 additional gates. The representation and cost are explicit-family bounds; they do not imply a polynomial-size transition on a succinct circuit description of the family or on arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Induction on prefix length using the coordinatewise filter; the per-coordinate predicate is constant after fixing the explicit family and level.

label: S0947
statement: RESIDUAL-STATE CHARACTERIZATION FOR FIXED-LENGTH STREAMING. Let L⊆{0,1}^N. For each t and p∈{0,1}^t, define R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N−t}: pz∈L}. In any deterministic streaming recognizer of L, two length-t prefixes can lead to the same state only if their residuals are equal; conversely, a recognizer with one state for each distinct residual at each depth recognizes L. Proof: If R_p≠R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference. Equal states after p and q would force identical acceptance on the common continuation z, contradicting that exactly one of pz,qz belongs to L. For the converse, transition the state R_p on bit b to R_{pb}={u:bu∈R_p}; at depth N accept iff the residual contains the empty string. Induction on the number of read bits shows the state after p is exactly R_p, so the machine recognizes L. This is a state characterization and gives no gate-cost bound for implementing transitions from H_C.

statement: FINITE-FAMILY PREFIX-PROJECTION CIRCUIT BOUND. Let C_1,...,C_M be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on N input bits, each with at most g fan-in-two gates. For a prefix p of length t define E(p)=1 iff there exist i in [M] and z in {0,1}^{N-t} such that C_i(pz)=1. Then E has a fan-in-two circuit with at most M 2^{N-t}(g+1)-1 gates, assuming constants and wiring are free. Any further fixed prefix cofactor satisfies the same bound with the shortened suffix length.
derivation: For every pair (i,z) in [M] x {0,1}^{N-t}, create a copy of C_i, hardwire p and z, and take the OR of all M 2^{N-t} outputs using a binary fan-in-two tree. This uses at most M 2^{N-t}g + (M 2^{N-t}-1) gates. Further hardwiring inputs cannot increase gate count.
scope: All finite N,M,g and prefixes p; explicit finite circuit family. No polynomial bound is asserted when M or 2^{N-t} grows.

statement: EXPLICIT-FAMILY OR AND COFACTOR BOUND. Let C_1,...,C_M be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on the same N input bits, each with at most g fan-in-two gates. The function F(x)=OR_{i=1}^M C_i(x) has a fan-in-two circuit with at most Mg+M-1 gates. For every fixed prefix p, the cofactor F_p has a circuit with at most the same number of gates.

statement:
statement: PREFIX LANGUAGE PARENT-CHILD RECURRENCE. Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length t<=N define E_L(p)=1 exactly when some string x in L extends p. If t<N, then E_L(p)=E_L(p0) OR E_L(p1). Consequently, if a circuit computes E_L on all prefixes at level t+1 (with p fixed and one suffix bit as input), the value at p is obtained by one OR gate from the two child acceptance bits; this recurrence alone does not compute either child predicate.
derivation: The completions of p are the disjoint union of strings extending p0 and strings extending p1. Thus at least one member of L extends p iff at least one of p0,p1 has an extension in L. The Boolean OR of the two indicator bits is exactly E_L(p).
scope: Every finite N, every language L subset {0,1}^N, every prefix p of length t<N. No circuit-size bound on computing E_L's child values is asserted.

statement:
statement: SURVIVING-DESCRIPTION DERIVATIVE LEMMA. Let D be a finite set of descriptions, each denoting a string f_d in {0,1}^N. For a prefix p of length t<N, define S(p)={d in D: f_d has prefix p}. For b in {0,1}, S(pb)={d in S(p): the (t+1)-st bit of f_d is b}. The residual language after p is exactly {suffix_t(f_d): d in S(p)}. Proof: By definition, d survives p iff its first t bits equal p. It survives pb iff its first t bits equal p and its next bit equals b, which is equivalent to d in S(p) with next bit b. A string q of length N-t is in the residual language after p iff pq=f_d for some d in D, equivalent to d surviving p and q being the remaining suffix. Thus filtering survivors computes the next semantic state, and projecting survivors gives the exact residual language. This does not bound the cost of representing S(p), grouping duplicate suffixes, or finding S(p) for circuit descriptions.
scope: All finite D and N, and every map d -> f_d in {0,1}^N. Semantic identity only; no succinct encoding or transition-cost bound.
derivation: Unpack prefix membership and concatenate p with a suffix q.
evidence: DISCOVERY run cm-71bbbc3708024dee checked 24 derivative cases and 17 residual classes for the four-string family in its code. The general result follows from the direct set-membership proof, not the finite run.

statement:
statement: FINITE-CANDIDATE TRIE STATE BOUND FOR EXT. Let D be a finite family of M binary words of common length N. For each prefix p of length at most N, define R(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pu is in D}. The prefix automaton with one state for each distinct nonempty residual R(p), plus a rejecting sink, recognizes D and has at most MN+2 states. Its transition on b from R(p) is R(pb)={u:bu is in R(p)}. It accepts at depth N precisely when R(p) is nonempty. Therefore its states admit an encoding of ceil(log2(MN+2)) bits. If D is generated by descriptions of length at most L, then the number of descriptions is less than 2^(L+1), so the encoding requires O(L+log N) bits. Proof: Each of the M words contributes at most N nonempty prefixes, hence at most MN nonempty trie nodes; include the root if needed and one rejecting sink. Merging nodes with equal residual languages does not increase the count. For any suffix u, u is in R(pb) exactly when pbu is in D, which holds exactly when bu is in R(p); this proves the transition identity. At depth N, the only suffix is empty, so residual nonemptiness is equivalent to p belonging to D. An injective index encoding uses ceil(log2 K) bits for K states. Counting descriptions gives M<2^(L+1), and thus log2(MN+2)=O(L+log N). This proves state size and exact transition semantics only; it gives no gate-cost bound for computing transitions from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.
derivation: Count prefixes in the trie, derive the child residual by concatenation, and encode the finite state set by an index. The circuit corollary counts descriptions, not distinct outputs.
scope: Every finite D subset of {0,1}^N, N>=1. The description corollary assumes an explicit binary encoding with at most 2^(L+1) descriptions of length at most L. No transition computation cost is asserted.

statement:
statement: EXT CANDIDATE FILTERING IDENTITY. Fix n,s and a finite set C_{n,s} of descriptions of Boolean circuits on n inputs of size at most s, with each description c computing f_c:{0,1}^N->{0,1}, N=2^n, the truth-table word in a fixed input order. For a prefix p of length t define A(p)={c in C_{n,s}: the first t bits of f_c equal p}. Then A(pb)={c in A(p): the (t+1)-st bit of f_c equals b}. The EXT residual language R(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: exists c in C_{n,s}, f_c=p||u} equals {suffix_t(f_c):c in A(p)}. Consequently EXT prefix state can be represented exactly by the surviving circuit descriptions A(p), and the next-bit update is a filter on their next output bit. Proof: By definition, c belongs to A(pb) iff its first t+1 output bits are p||b, which is equivalent to its first t bits being p and its next bit being b; this proves the filter identity. A suffix u belongs to R(p) iff there exists c with f_c=p||u, equivalently c belongs to A(p) and its remaining suffix is u; this proves the residual identity. The argument is finite and exact. It gives neither a succinct representation of A(p) beyond listing descriptions nor a bound on the real-gate cost of filtering it, and therefore does not imply a transition-cost reduction for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Expand the definitions of the image prefix residual and the surviving-description set; split equality of output prefixes at the (t+1)th bit.
scope: Any finite circuit-description set C_{n,s}, fixed output truth-table order, and all prefixes of lengths 0 through N. No uniformity or efficient-update bound asserted.

A suffix u belongs to R(p) iff there exists c with f_c=p||u, equivalently c belongs to A(p) and its remaining suffix is u; this proves the residual identity. The argument is finite and exact. It gives neither a succinct representation of A(p) beyond listing descriptions nor a bound on the real-gate cost of filtering it, and therefore does not imply a transition-cost reduction for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Expand the definitions of the image prefix residual and the surviving-description set; split equality of output prefixes at the (t+1)th bit.
scope: Any finite circuit-description set C_{n,s}, fixed output truth-table order, and all prefixes of lengths 0 through N. No uniformity or efficient-update bound asserted.

label: S0961
statement:
statement: FINITE CANDIDATE-AGREEMENT AUTOMATON WITH EXPLICIT UPDATE COST. Let N be a nonnegative integer and F=(f_1,...,f_M) an ordered finite family of strings in {0,1}^N, allowing M=0 and repetitions. For each t in {0,...,N}, each prefix p in {0,1}^t, and each i, define q_t(i)=1 iff the first t bits of f_i equal p. The vector q_t is an exact state for the surviving candidates; p has an extension in F iff OR_i q_t(i)=1. Given p's next bit b at position t+1, the transition is q_{t+1}(i)=q_t(i) AND [f_i(t+1)=b] for every i. With F and the position-dependent constants fixed in the transition, this is implemented by at most M fan-in-two AND gates. Proof: At t=0 the empty prefix agrees with every f_i, so the stated invariant holds. Assume it holds at t. A candidate f_i agrees with the length-(t+1) prefix pb exactly when it agrees with p and its (t+1)-st bit equals b. This equivalence is precisely the displayed update, so induction proves the invariant for all t. The prefix has an extension in F exactly when at least one candidate agrees with it, which is equivalent to OR_i q_t(i)=1; for M=0 this OR is the constant 0. Each coordinate update is either q_t(i) AND 1, or q_t(i) AND 0, according to the fixed candidate bit and b; one AND gate per coordinate suffices (and constants may simplify it). This proves the transition bound. The result gives no compression of the M-bit state, no useful bound on M in terms of circuit size parameters, and no representation or transition bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.
derivation: Induction on prefix length using the exact equivalence: candidate i matches pb iff it matches p and its next bit is b. The extendibility output is the OR of the agreement coordinates. Implement each coordinate by one AND with the appropriate fixed comparison bit.
scope: Every finite N, every ordered finite family F subset {0,1}^N including the empty family and repeated strings, and every prefix length 0<=t<=N; explicit M-coordinate representation only.

label: S0962
statement:
statement: RIGHT-RESIDUAL CHARACTERIZATION OF EXACT PREFIX STATES. Let L be any finite binary language and, for each prefix p, define R_p={z in {0,1}*: pz is a prefix of some word in L}. In any deterministic prefix-processing automaton that exactly tracks whether the current prefix can be extended to a word in L, two prefixes assigned the same state must have equal right residuals R_p. Conversely, equality R_p=R_q permits identifying p and q while preserving all future extendibility answers. Thus the minimal exact state partition is equality of right residuals; the number of required states is the number of distinct sets R_p.
derivation: For necessity, if z belongs to exactly one of R_p and R_q, then after reading z the exact extendibility answer differs, whereas a deterministic automaton starting from the same state and reading the same z must reach the same state and answer identically, a contradiction. For sufficiency, if R_p=R_q, then for every continuation z the extendibility answers agree by definition, so merging p and q preserves every future answer. Equality of residuals is therefore both necessary and sufficient for state equivalence, and the quotient by that equivalence is the minimal exact partition.
scope: Every finite binary language L, including the finite language Im(Eval_{n,s}) defining EXT_{n,s}. This characterizes state information only; it gives no bound on transition time or on real-gate operations over H_C.

label: S0963
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL DERIVATIVE GIVES A WELL-DEFINED DETERMINISTIC TRANSITION. Let L be any language over {0,1}, and for each finite string p define R_p={z in {0,1}*: pz is a prefix of some word in L}. For every prefix p and bit b, R_{pb}={z: bz in R_p}. Consequently, if R_p=R_q then R_{pb}=R_{qb} for each bit b, so the quotient whose states are distinct residuals has well-defined transitions delta(R_p,b)=R_{pb}. Proof: For any z, z is in R_{pb} iff pbz is a prefix of a word in L. By associativity of concatenation, this holds iff b z is in R_p. This proves the set identity. If R_p=R_q, then for every z, bz belongs to R_p iff bz belongs to R_q; applying the identity gives z in R_{pb} iff z in R_{qb}, hence equality. Therefore the transition on residual equivalence classes is independent of the representative prefix. For finite L, only finitely many distinct residuals occur: a prefix longer than every word of L has empty residual, and the remaining prefixes are finite in number. Scope: semantic state transitions for every finite binary language; no circuit-size or real-gate transition-cost bound is claimed.
derivation: For each z, membership in R_{pb} means pbz is a prefix of some word in L, which is equivalent to bz being in R_p. Equality of input residuals therefore implies equality of their derivatives, making quotient transitions representative-independent.
scope: Every finite binary language; this is a semantic residual transition lemma only, with no bound on computing transitions for EXT or on arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

structure.gap: The assigned EXT-versus-H_C connection still lacks a bound on the real-gate cost of implementing an EXT residual transition from H_C, and no implication for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits has been established.
