label: S0964
statement:
statement: DISTINCT CONTINUATION RESIDUALS REQUIRE DISTINCT EXACT STREAMING STATES. Let L be any language over {0,1}, and for each prefix p let R_p={z in {0,1}*: pz is a prefix of a word in L}. Suppose a deterministic streaming recognizer has state set Q, starts in q0, updates by a function δ:Q×{0,1}→Q, and after reading a prefix p its state determines whether p is extendible to a word of L. Then R_p≠R_q implies the states reached after p and q are different. Consequently |Q|≥|{R_p:p∈{0,1}*}|, and any fixed-length binary encoding of its states needs at least ceil(log2 |{R_p}|) bits. Proof: Suppose R_p≠R_q. There is a string z belonging to exactly one of these two sets. By the definition of R, exactly one of pz and qz is a prefix of a word in L. If the recognizer reached the same state after p and q, determinism implies that reading the same continuation z leads to the same final state in both runs, hence the same extendibility answer, a contradiction. Thus every pair of distinct residuals has distinct reached states. The state-count and bit-count bounds follow by injection. Scope: exact deterministic streaming recognition of prefix extendibility for any language; this lower bound says nothing about transition cost in real gates or randomized recognizers.
derivation: For distinct residual sets choose a distinguishing continuation z. Same state after p and q would, under the same deterministic transitions on z, force identical answers, contradicting that z belongs to exactly one residual. Therefore residual classes inject into states.
scope: All languages over {0,1}; deterministic exact streaming recognition only. No circuit-cost or MCSP lower bound.

structure.gap: This information lower bound does not resolve the remaining G0206 issue: whether the EXT residual transition can be implemented from H_C at bounded real-gate cost, nor whether such a representation applies to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0965
statement:
statement: CANONICAL CANDIDATE-SET AUTOMATON FOR EXT. Fix n,s and a finite canonical circuit-description set D_{n,s} containing a description for every Boolean function on n bits computable by a circuit of size at most s. Order the 2^n truth-table inputs as x_1,...,x_{2^n}. For each prefix p of length t, let A_p={d in D_{n,s}: the function computed by d agrees with p on x_1,...,x_t}. Then p is extendible iff A_p is nonempty, and after reading next bit b the exact update is A_{pb}={d in A_p: d(x_{t+1})=b}. Proof: By definition, d agrees with pb precisely when it agrees with p on the first t positions and has value b at x_{t+1}; hence the displayed equality. Induction on t shows that the state maintained after p is exactly A_p, and nonemptiness is equivalent to a size-at-most-s circuit realizing a completion of p. The subset representation uses |D_{n,s}| membership bits and can be updated directly by evaluating each candidate description at x_{t+1} and filtering. This gives no lower bound on information required by alternate encodings and no polynomial real-gate transition bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: The state is the set of all bounded-size circuit descriptions consistent with the observed prefix. The next bit filters this set by its value on the next truth-table input. The definition proves the update identity and induction proves exact recognition.
scope: Every n,s, finite canonical description set complete for size-at-most-s functions, and every fixed truth-table ordering.

label: S0966
statement:
statement: FINITE-FAMILY PREFIX-MASK UPDATE. Let F={f_1,...,f_K} be a finite indexed family of Boolean functions on {0,1}^N. For a prefix p, define M(p)_i=1 exactly when f_i agrees with p on all positions of p. If p has length t<N and b∈{0,1}, define M(pb)_i=M(p)_i AND [f_i(p_1...p_t)=b]. Then M(pb) is exactly the mask of functions agreeing with pb, including when M(p) is empty. The update uses at most K AND gates once the K next-output bits are available; testing whether any candidate remains takes at most K−1 OR gates. Proof: For each i, agreement with pb holds iff agreement with p holds and f_i’s bit at position t+1 equals b. This is precisely the stated bitwise update, coordinate by coordinate. The acceptance test is the OR of the K mask bits, implemented by a binary OR tree. Scope is a fixed, explicitly indexed finite family; this gives no bound on computing the next-output bits from a compressed state and no useful polynomial bound when K is large.
derivation: Coordinatewise, f_i agrees with pb iff f_i agrees with p and its next bit is b; the acceptance test is the OR of the mask coordinates.
scope: All finite K,N and prefixes of length t<N. This is a finite-family representation lemma only; it does not bound transitions for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits or close the EXT-versus-H_C connection.

label: S0967
statement:
statement: BOUNDED-WITNESS PROJECTION AND COFACTOR BOUND. Let H(x,w) be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates, where x has N bits and w has r bits. Define G(x)=1 iff there exists w in {0,1}^r with H(x,w)=1. For any fixed r, G has a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2^r(h+1)-1 gates. For any prefix p of x and next bit b, the cofactors G_p and G_{pb} have circuits no larger than this bound. Consequently, for each fixed constant k, projections with r<=k have circuits of size at most 2^k(h+1)-1, and fixing any prefix bits is implementable by hardwiring with zero additional gates.
derivation: For each of the 2^r assignments a to w, copy H and hardwire w=a, giving a circuit H_a(x) of at most h gates. A binary OR tree on the 2^r outputs uses 2^r-1 gates, so their disjunction computes G with at most 2^r h+2^r-1=2^r(h+1)-1 gates. This disjunction equals G by the definition of existential quantification over {0,1}^r. Hardwiring any prefix p or next bit b in this circuit removes inputs and cannot add gates; the resulting circuit computes the corresponding cofactor. If r<=k, the bound is at most 2^k(h+1)-1.
scope: All finite Boolean fan-in-two circuits H; constants and input wiring free. The linear-in-h consequence assumes witness width r bounded by fixed constant k. Does not imply a useful bound when r grows, nor bridge arbitrary MCSP decision circuits or P vs NP.

label: S0968
statement:
statement: FACTORISED WITNESS PROJECTION WITH SHARED INPUTS. Let H(x,w_1,...,w_k)=AND_{i=1}^k H_i(x,w_i), where each H_i is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h_i gates and w_i has r_i bits. Then G(x)=1 iff there exist w_1,...,w_k such that H(x,w_1,...,w_k)=1 has a fan-in-two circuit of at most sum_i(2^{r_i}(h_i+1)-1)+(k-1) gates. The same bound holds for every cofactor of G obtained by fixing input bits.
derivation: Because the witness blocks are disjoint and H is their conjunction, for each fixed x, there exist w_1,...,w_k with AND_i H_i(x,w_i)=1 iff for every i there exists w_i with H_i(x,w_i)=1. For each i, enumerate its 2^{r_i} witness assignments, hardwire each assignment into a copy of H_i, and OR the outputs with a binary tree. This constructs G_i(x)=exists w_i H_i(x,w_i) using at most 2^{r_i}h_i+(2^{r_i}-1)=2^{r_i}(h_i+1)-1 gates. AND the k outputs using k-1 gates. The resulting circuit computes G and has the stated size. Fixing input bits in that circuit cannot increase its gate count, so the same upper bound applies to every cofactor.
scope: All finite fan-in-two Boolean circuits with the displayed conjunction factorization; blocks may share visible inputs x but have pairwise disjoint witness variables. Constants and input wiring are free. No claim that arbitrary verifiers admit this factorization, and no growing-witness bound beyond the displayed sum.

label: S0969
statement:
statement: COMPUTABLE-WITNESS ELIMINATION LEMMA. Let H(x,w) be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates and D(x) compute r witness bits by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of d gates. Suppose for every x, (exists w H(x,w)=1) iff H(x,D(x))=1. Then G(x)=exists w H(x,w) has a fan-in-two circuit with at most h+d gates.
derivation: Build D and connect its r output wires to the witness inputs of H, retaining H's visible-input wires. The composed circuit computes H(x,D(x)), which equals the existential projection by the stated hypothesis, and uses at most d+h gates.
scope: All finite input and witness lengths; fan-in-two circuits; the equality hypothesis is required for every visible input. For fixed deterministic circuit tableaux, D is the gate-evaluation map, so the lemma eliminates tableau witnesses with linear overhead. It gives no bound for witnesses encoding a search over candidate circuits.

structure.gap: The general EXT residual-transition cost from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit remains open: this lemma applies only when the witness can itself be computed by a small circuit.

label: S0970
statement: statement: BOUNDED-WITNESS PROJECTION COST. Let H(x,w) be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates, with constants and wiring free, and let w range over {0,1}^r. The existential projection G(x)=1 iff there exists w in {0,1}^r with H(x,w)=1 has a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^r(h+1)-1 gates. Consequently, if h(s) is polynomial in s and r(s)=O(log s), then G has polynomial size in s. This bound alone gives no polynomial-size conclusion when r is not O(log s). Proof: For every assignment a in {0,1}^r, make a separate copy H_a of H with w fixed to a. Each copy computes x -> H(x,a) using at most h gates. OR the 2^r outputs with a binary OR tree using 2^r-1 gates. Total size is 2^r h + 2^r - 1 = 2^r(h+1)-1. If r(s) <= c log_2(s)+d and h(s)<=s^k for fixed c,d,k, this is at most 2^d s^c(s^k+1)-1, a polynomial in s. For unbounded larger r this expression may be superpolynomial, so no such conclusion follows from this construction.

label: S0971
statement:
statement: EXPLICIT CIRCUIT-ENUMERATION CIRCUIT FOR EXT PREFIX TESTS. Fix n>=1, N=2^n, a fixed encoding of fan-in-two Boolean circuits on n inputs with at most s gates, and let D_{n,s} be its set of valid descriptions, of cardinality M. For a prefix p of length t, EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff some d in D_{n,s} computes a truth table whose first t bits equal p. There is a Boolean circuit deciding EXT_{n,s}(p), with p as input and n,s,t fixed, of size O(M*t*(s+1)+M), under the convention that description wiring/constant bits are free and candidate circuits are evaluated by their gate equations. Specifically, for each d form the conjunction over i<t of [C_d(i)=p_i], then OR these M conjunctions. Therefore the child predicate EXT_{n,s}(p b) is decided by the same construction with t+1 positions; the algorithmic description is an explicit transition test, with circuit size proportional to the number of descriptions, rather than an existential suffix projection.
derivation: For each valid description d, compute C_d(i) for every fixed index i<t by evaluating its gates in topological order. Each gate contributes O(1) Boolean gates per evaluation, hence all t outputs for d cost O(t(s+1)) gates (the fixed input i is hardwired, and p_i is wired into the equality test). Conjoin the t equality bits, using O(t) gates. OR the resulting M acceptance bits with M-1 gates. The resulting output is 1 exactly when at least one valid description agrees with p at every one of its t coordinates, which is exactly the definition of EXT_{n,s}(p). Replacing t by t+1 proves the child test. This construction makes no polynomial-in-s claim because M may be exponential in s log(n+s).
scope: All fixed n,s,t with 0<=t<=2^n, for the explicitly fixed finite circuit-description encoding; it is an ordinary Boolean circuit in the prefix bits. It supplies an explicit but potentially exponential description-enumeration cost and does not bound transitions for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0973
statement:
statement: DEPTH-SUM PREFIX RESIDUAL BOUND. Let N be a nonnegative integer and L be a finite subset of {0,1}^N. For each 0<=t<=N and each p in {0,1}^t, define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}, and let d_t be the number of distinct nonempty sets R_p at depth t. Then d_t <= min(2^t, |L|), and the total number of distinct residual states across all depths, counting the empty residual separately at each depth, is at most (N+1)+sum_{t=0}^N min(2^t,|L|). Proof: There are 2^t prefixes, so d_t<=2^t. Let P_t be the prefixes with nonempty residual. For every p in P_t choose z_p in R_p. The map p -> pz_p is injective into L because its image has prefix p, hence |P_t|<=|L|. Since the number of distinct nonempty residuals is at most |P_t|, d_t<=|L|. At each depth there is at most one empty residual, so adding it contributes at most N+1 states over all depths. Summing the per-depth bounds proves the result. For L=Im(Eval_{n,s}), this bounds the total canonical prefix-automaton state count by (N+1)+sum_t min(2^t,|Im(Eval_{n,s})|), but says nothing about the cost of computing transitions or whether this quantity is polynomial in n,s.
derivation: At each t, nonempty residuals are no more numerous than their prefixes; selecting a member suffix injects those prefixes into L. Add at most one empty residual per depth and sum.

label: S0974
statement:
statement: statement: EXPLICIT PREFIX-TRIE TRANSITION BOUND. Let N>=0 and L be any subset of {0,1}^N with M=|L|. The prefix trie has at most 1+NM nodes and NM directed edges. It recognizes L with a deterministic finite automaton using at most 2+NM states, counting one rejecting sink. Proof: Each word contributes at most N nonempty prefixes, so their union has at most NM nodes; adjoining the empty root gives at most 1+NM trie nodes. Every nonroot trie node has exactly one incoming edge, so there are at most NM edges. Add one rejecting sink; from each trie node on bit b follow the b-edge if present and otherwise enter the sink, and let exactly the length-N word nodes be accepting. This deterministic automaton accepts exactly L. Its states can be encoded using ceil(log2(2+NM)) bits. This is a finite-state transition-table construction, not a Boolean circuit size bound for implementing the transition function.
derivation: Count at most N nonempty prefixes per word and take their union; each nonroot trie node corresponds to exactly one edge; add a sink and define transitions by trie edges or sink, with accepting nodes precisely L.
scope: All finite N>=0 and L subset {0,1}^N; gives state count and an explicit transition table only, without circuit complexity guarantees.

label: S0975
statement:
statement: EXACT PREFIX RECURRENCE FOR A FIXED CIRCUIT. Let C:{0,1}^N→{0,1} be a Boolean circuit, and let H_C(x,y) be its local tableau verifier, with y containing one output bit per gate. For each prefix p of length t≤N, define E_C(p)=1 iff there are z∈{0,1}^{N−t} and y such that H_C(pz,y)=1. Then E_C(p)=E_C(p0)∨E_C(p1) for t<N, and E_C(p)=C(p) for t=N. Also, for every p, E_C(p)=1 iff some completion x of p satisfies C(x)=1. Proof: The gate equations in H_C uniquely force y to be the evaluation of C on its input, by induction in topological gate order. Thus H_C(x,y)=1 for some y exactly when C(x)=1. For t<N, every completion of p has a unique first suffix bit b∈{0,1} and a remaining suffix z′; hence a satisfying completion of p exists exactly when a satisfying completion of p0 or p1 exists. At t=N the only completion is p itself, giving E_C(p)=C(p). This establishes exact information and its recurrence; it makes no bound on the ordinary-circuit cost of computing E_C from a representation of H_C.
derivation: Use uniqueness of the local gate-evaluation tableau to replace existential quantification over y by C(x)=1. Partition all completions of a nonterminal prefix according to their next bit; at a full-length prefix there is only that input.
scope: All finite N and all fixed Boolean circuits C; fan-in is unrestricted for the recurrence, provided H_C correctly encodes C. This is a semantic identity, not a transition-cost or MCSP lower-bound claim.

statement:
statement: FINITE-FAMILY PREFIX FILTER TRANSITION. Let N,K be positive integers and let C_1,...,C_K be explicitly listed Boolean functions on {0,1}^N (equivalently, K fixed truth tables). Define Q(p)={i in [K] : C_i[1..t]=p} for each prefix p of length t. On reading b at position t+1, update q_i to q_i AND [C_i[t+1]=b]. The update is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most K AND gates, with the comparison bits fixed by the family and position. For every prefix p, the maintained set is exactly Q(p), so Q(p) is nonempty iff p is extendible by a member of the listed family. Proof: Initially Q(empty)=[K]. If the invariant holds at length t, then an index remains after the update exactly when its function matched p and its next truth-table bit equals b, which is equivalent to matching p concatenated with b. Induction proves the invariant at every length. Each coordinate update uses one AND gate with a fixed comparison bit, hence at most K gates per transition. This statement gives no polynomial bound in s when K is the full family of size-s circuit descriptions.
scope: All finite N,K and any explicitly listed family of K Boolean truth tables; transition circuit uses the candidate-membership vector as its state and position-dependent fixed comparison bits.

statement: statement: DISTINCT-WITNESS-COFACTOR PROJECTION BOUND. Let H(x,w) be a Boolean function with w in {0,1}^r. Suppose the distinct functions among H_w(x)=H(x,w) are d functions, each computable by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most h gates. Then G(x)=exists w H(x,w) has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most d(h+1)-1 gates. Proof: Choose one witness assignment for each distinct cofactor function. Compute those d functions with separate circuits, then OR their outputs in a binary tree using d-1 additional gates. The resulting function is exactly G because duplicate cofactors do not change a disjunction. This bound gives no claim that d is small or efficiently computable.

statement: statement: PREFIX RESTRICTION MONOTONICITY FOR WITNESS COFACTOR COUNTS. Let H(x,w) be any Boolean function and, for each prefix p, define F_{p,w}(z)=H(pz,w). Let d_p be the number of distinct functions F_{p,w} over all witnesses w. For every next bit b, d_{pb} <= d_p. Proof: restriction R_b sends each parent function f(z) to f(bz'), and every child function is its parent's image under this map. Hence the child set is an image of the parent set, whose cardinality cannot increase. This is semantic; it asserts no efficient way to compute the classes or representatives.

statement: statement: BOUNDED-REMAINING-SUFFIX COFACTOR ENUMERATION. Let H:{0,1}^{t+q}×W→{0,1}, where W is finite, and let h be the gate size of a circuit for H. Given prefix p of length t, one can construct the exact projected cofactor G_p(z)=∨_{w∈W}H(pz,w) by enumerating all w and all z∈{0,1}^q, storing each truth table, deduplicating identical tables, and OR-ing one representative per distinct table. The construction uses O(|W|2^q(h+q+1)) time and at most d(h+1)-1 output gates, where d is the number of distinct cofactor tables. Proof: direct evaluation fills each table; equality of finite bit strings decides functional equality on the q-bit domain; deduplication preserves the disjunction; a binary OR tree combines the d retained functions. This is useful when |W|2^q is polynomial in the parameters, and gives no bound when q or |W| is large.

statement: statement: RESIDUAL-LANGUAGE CHARACTERIZATION OF EXACT EXT STATES. Fix n,s and let T be the set of truth tables of Boolean circuits on n inputs of size at most s. For every prefix p of length t, define R_p={z in {0,1}^{2^n-t}: pz is in T}. In any deterministic exact streaming algorithm deciding whether each received prefix extends to a member of T, prefixes p,q that reach the same internal state must satisfy R_p=R_q. Conversely, the state R_p, updated on bit b by R_{pb}={z: bz is in R_p}, is sufficient to decide extendibility by testing whether R_p is nonempty. Proof: if R_p and R_q differ, choose z in their symmetric difference; after the identical continuation z, exactly one of pz,qz is extendible, so a deterministic machine in the same state could not answer both correctly. The update formula follows directly by decomposing a completing suffix after its first bit. This characterizes required information, but gives no compact encoding or efficient update bound.

structure.gap: The residual-language characterization is exact but does not bound the number of residuals or provide a compact representation/update. Determine a size or update bound for a specified encoding, or connect this characterization to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits with a proved transition-cost relation.

statement:
statement: RESIDUAL-STATE CHARACTERIZATION FOR FIXED-LENGTH LANGUAGES. Let N be a nonnegative integer and L be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length t<=N define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz is in L}. Any deterministic exact recognizer that reads bits left to right and decides membership in L must be in different states after any two length-t prefixes p,q with R_p != R_q. Conversely, a recognizer whose states at depth t are the distinct residual sets R_p, and whose transition on b maps R_p to {z: bz in R_p}, decides L exactly. Thus the minimum number of reachable states at depth t is exactly the number of distinct residuals at that depth.
derivation: Necessity: if R_p and R_q differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. If the machine had the same state after p and q, its deterministic continuation on z would have the same result, although exactly one of pz,qz belongs to L, contradiction. Sufficiency: after reading p, store R_p. On reading b, the residual becomes R_pb={z: pbz in L}={z: bz in R_p}, so the transition rule preserves the invariant that the state is the residual of the prefix read. At depth N the residual contains only the empty string when the full word is in L; accept in exactly that case. The two inequalities give the exact minimum state count.
scope: All finite fixed-length binary languages and every depth 0<=t<=N. The statement concerns abstract deterministic states; it gives no circuit-size bound for encoding residuals or implementing transitions, in particular no bounded-cost transformation from arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

statement: FIXED-DEPTH EXT RESIDUAL COUNT. Let F be a finite subset of {0,1}^N and 0 <= t <= N. For p in {0,1}^t define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}. Then the number of distinct sets R_p is at most |F|+1.
derivation: Let P+ be the length-t prefixes p with R_p nonempty. For each p in P+, choose f_p in F whose length-t prefix is p. Distinct prefixes yield distinct chosen words, so p -> f_p is injective and |P+| <= |F|. Every nonempty residual is realized by a prefix in P+, hence there are at most |F| distinct nonempty residuals. All empty residuals equal the empty set, adding at most one more. Thus the total is at most |F|+1. Distinct residual sets need not be disjoint; the proof uses only the injection from viable prefixes to F.
scope: All finite F subseteq {0,1}^N and all 0 <= t <= N; a state-count bound for the exact prefix automaton.

label: S0985
statement:
statement: RESIDUALS ARE EXACTLY THE FUTURE DISTINGUISHERS. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length t<=N define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}. Any deterministic left-to-right streaming recognizer correct for F must be in different internal states after prefixes p and q whenever R_p != R_q. If R_p=R_q, then p and q have the same acceptance outcome for every common suffix.
derivation: If R_p=R_q, then for every suffix z, pz is in F iff z is in R_p iff z is in R_q iff qz is in F. If R_p!=R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference. Exactly one of pz and qz is in F. If a deterministic recognizer were in the same state after p and q, processing the same suffix z from that state would produce the same final output on both inputs, contradicting correctness. Thus different residuals require different states, and equal residuals have identical future acceptance behavior. This identifies the exact future-membership information at depth t, without bounding the cost of computing transitions or total state count.
scope: All N>=0, F subseteq {0,1}^N, and fixed depths 0<=t<=N; deterministic left-to-right streaming recognizers with a common transition rule and correct final membership output.

label: S0986
statement:
statement: EXT STATE-BIT BOUND FROM CIRCUIT DESCRIPTIONS. Fix n,s>=0. Let F_{n,s} be the set of truth tables on {0,1}^n computed by Boolean circuits with at most s fan-in-at-most-two gates, where each gate is one of the 16 Boolean functions of two inputs, inputs may be chosen from the n variables, constants 0 and 1, or earlier gate outputs, and one output wire is selected. For every prefix depth t in [0,2^n], the number of distinct EXT residuals R_p={z in {0,1}^{2^n-t}: pz in F_{n,s}} is at most |F_{n,s}|+1, and hence can be represented by at most ceil(log2(|F_{n,s}|+1)) bits. In particular, this is O((s+1)log(n+s+2)) bits.
derivation: Put A=16(n+s+2)^2. A circuit with exactly k gates, for 0<=k<=s, has at most A^k possible ordered descriptions: for each gate there are 16 choices of Boolean function and at most (n+s+2)^2 choices of ordered input wires, an upper bound that allows unavailable future wires and therefore only overcounts. Its output wire has at most n+s+2 choices. Thus the number D of descriptions of circuits of size at most s is at most (n+s+2) sum_{k=0}^s A^k <= (s+1)(n+s+2)A^s. Every truth table in F_{n,s} has at least one such description, so |F_{n,s}|<=D. At depth t, each prefix with nonempty residual has an extension in F_{n,s}; choosing one extension for each such prefix is injective because distinct prefixes cannot be prefixes of the same word. Hence there are at most |F_{n,s}| distinct nonempty residuals, and all empty residuals coincide, giving at most |F_{n,s}|+1 residuals total. The required fixed-width encoding takes ceil(log2(|F_{n,s}|+1)) bits. Finally, log2(D+1)=O((s+1)log(n+s+2)) from the displayed bound and A=16(n+s+2)^2. This proves the claimed state-bit bound. It supplies no circuit for computing a residual transition from H_C and no transition gate-cost bound.
scope: All n,s>=0, this explicit fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuit description model, and each fixed prefix depth. A bound on the number of semantic automaton states only; no claim about transition complexity or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0987
statement:
statement: POLYNOMIAL-CARDINALITY CIRCUIT-UNION PROJECTION LEMMA. Let F={C_1,...,C_M} be a nonempty finite family of Boolean circuits on common input x, each with at most h fan-in-two gates; allow constants and input wiring for free. Define U(x)=1 iff C_i(x)=1 for some i. Then U has a fan-in-two circuit with at most M(h+1)-1 gates. For every fixed input prefix p, the cofactor U_p has a circuit with at most the same number of gates, and fixing one more input bit to obtain U_{pb} does not increase this bound. Consequently, if M and h are polynomially bounded in a parameter, then U and all its prefix cofactors have polynomial-size circuits. Proof: Copy each C_i separately and combine their outputs using a binary OR tree. The copies use at most Mh gates, and the OR tree uses M-1 gates, for a total Mh+M-1=M(h+1)-1. Substituting fixed prefix bits in a circuit only replaces input wires by constants, so cannot increase the number of gates; this applies again to the next bit. Polynomially bounded M and h make the displayed product polynomial. This lemma applies to an explicitly enumerable finite family; it gives no polynomial-size bound when M is exponential, as in the unrestricted family of size-s circuits.
derivation: For each member circuit take a disjoint copy; join the M outputs by a binary OR tree; hardwire prefix bits in the resulting circuit. The gate count is Mh+(M-1), and cofactors cannot have larger gate count.
scope: All integers M>=1,h>=0 and all finite families of Boolean circuits over a fan-in-two basis containing OR, with constants and input wiring free. Does not bound unrestricted EXT when its candidate family is exponential.

label: S0988
statement:
statement: EXT RESIDUAL CHARACTERIZATION. Let F be a finite family of Boolean functions on N-bit inputs, with truth tables in a fixed order, and let p be a prefix of length t that occurs as the first t bits of at least one member of F. Define R(p)={u in {0,1}^{2^N-t}: pu is the truth table of some f in F}. For V(p)={f in F: the truth table of f begins with p}, R(p) is exactly the union, over f in V(p), of the suffixes of f's truth table after position t. Consequently two occurring prefixes p,q (possibly of different lengths) have identical residual completion languages if and only if these unions of suffixes are equal. In particular, equality of candidate sets implies equality of residual languages, but equality of candidate sets is not necessary. Proof: A suffix u belongs to R(p) iff pu is the truth table of some f in F. This is equivalent to f belonging to V(p) and u being exactly the suffix of f after the prefix p. Taking the union over V(p) gives the first equality. Applying that equality to p and q proves the stated iff. The candidate-set map therefore gives a sufficient, possibly nonminimal, representation of the residual language.
derivation: Unpack membership in the residual completion language: an extension pu is a member truth table exactly when a family member has prefix p and suffix u. This is exactly the union of suffixes over V(p). Equality of residuals is therefore equivalent to equality of those unions; the map from candidate sets to unions can identify different sets.
scope: Every finite family of Boolean functions with a fixed truth-table order and every occurring prefix. This is an information characterization only; it makes no gate-complexity or transition-cost claim.

label: S0989
statement: statement: FINITE ENUMERATION TRANSITION CIRCUIT BOUND. Let F={w_1,...,w_M} be an explicitly listed set of distinct binary strings of common length L, and let D_t be the distinct length-t prefixes of strings in F. Encode each live prefix by an injective index in {0,...,|D_t|-1}, and reserve one additional index for dead. For each fixed t<L, the exact next-prefix transition (state i, input bit b) to the index of the length-(t+1) prefix if it exists in D_{t+1}, else dead, is computable by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O((M+1)log(M+1)) gates, with constants and wiring free. Proof: There are at most M live indices and one dead index. For each live i and b, the explicit list F determines a unique target index j or dead. A binary equality comparator between the state bits and fixed index i uses O(log(M+1)) gates; AND with the input literal selects the corresponding row. OR the selected indicators for each output bit, using O(M log(M+1)) gates in total, and similarly form dead's code. The dead row maps to dead and costs O(log(M+1)) gates. Since |D_t|<=M, the total is O((M+1)log(M+1)). This proves a transition circuit conditional on the family being explicitly listed; it does not bound the cost of generating that list, and for all size-<=s circuits M may be exponential in s log(n+s).

structure.evidence: A direct transition-table implementation uses at most M live indices plus a dead state and O(log(M+1)) bits. For each state and input bit the list specifies one target; selecting these rows and ORing target-code bits costs O(M log(M+1)) fan-in-two gates. This is a constructive upper bound for explicitly listed F only.

label: S0990
statement: statement: RESIDUAL-INDEXED TRANSITION CIRCUIT BOUND. Let F be a finite set of distinct binary strings of common length L. For 0<=t<L, let R_t be the set of distinct nonempty residual suffix languages after length-t prefixes, and let r_t=|R_t|. Index these states and reserve a dead state. The exact one-bit transition from a state R in R_t and bit b to {u: bu in R}, or to dead if this set is empty, has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O((r_t+1) log(r_t+2)) gates, with constants and wiring free. The transition table can be constructed from an explicit listing of F. Proof: For each R and b, its child {u:bu in R} depends only on R, not on the prefix representing it. It is therefore a unique member of R_{t+1} or empty. Decode each state code with an equality comparator, select the target code according to b, and OR the selected target bits for each output bit. There are 2r_t live rows, O(log(r_t+2)) code bits, and O(log(r_t+2)) gates per row/output selection, so the total is O((r_t+1) log(r_t+2)); add a dead row mapping to dead. This bounds circuit size only; table generation may depend on |F| and no polynomial bound follows for an implicit circuit family.

structure.evidence: Each target is the left quotient {u:bu in R}, determined solely by the residual language R. A direct decoded transition table therefore has 2r_t live rows and O(log(r_t+2)) bits per code.

label: S0991
statement: statement: PREFIX-MATCHING RELATION FROM A UNIVERSAL EVALUATOR. Let D be a finite set of descriptions, let P(d) be a Boolean predicate selecting the valid size-at-most-s candidates, and let U(d,x) be a Boolean circuit of u gates that outputs the truth-table bit of the circuit described by d on input x whenever P(d)=1. For any ordered list x_0,...,x_{k-1} of distinct inputs and bit string a in {0,1}^k, there is a Boolean circuit V_a(d) of at most k(u+1)+v+O(k) fan-in-two gates, where v is the size of P, such that V_a(d)=1 exactly when P(d)=1 and U(d,x_i)=a_i for every i<k. Consequently, existence of a size-at-most-s circuit matching the selected k truth-table positions is exactly the existential statement ∃d V_a(d)=1. Proof: Make k copies of U with x_i hardwired, negate each output whose desired bit a_i is 0, and AND all k literals with P(d). Hardwiring x_i adds no gates; each output negation costs at most one gate, and a fan-in-two conjunction of k+1 terms costs at most k gates. Thus the stated bound holds. The conclusion is an existential circuit encoding, not a procedure for eliminating d or producing an ordinary small circuit for the projected predicate on a.

structure.evidence: This is a direct circuit construction from the stated universal evaluator and validity predicate; no claim is made that existential projection has comparable circuit size.

label: S0992
statement:
statement: DISTINCT-WITNESS-COFACTOR CIRCUIT BOUND. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates. For each w∈{0,1}^r define H_w(x)=H(x,w), and let q be the number of distinct Boolean functions among the H_w. Then G(x)=∃w H(x,w) has a fan-in-two circuit with at most qh+q−1 gates. For every fixed prefix p of the visible input x, the cofactor G_p has a circuit with at most qh+q−1 gates. Proof: Choose one witness representative for each distinct function H_w. For each of the q representatives, copy the circuit for H and hardwire that witness, using at most qh gates total. The OR of the q outputs is exactly ∨_w H_w(x), since every witness function occurs among the representatives; a binary OR tree uses q−1 gates. Hardwiring a visible prefix in this circuit cannot increase its gate count. This is an existence bound only: it gives no efficient method to find representatives and no bound on q for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Partition the 2^r witnesses by equality of their induced functions H_w. A representative from each class suffices because existential projection is the disjunction of these functions. Implement each representative by one hardwired copy of H (qh gates total), then combine with q−1 OR gates. Cofactoring visible inputs is substitution and cannot increase size.
scope: All finite N,r,h; fan-in-two Boolean circuits with constants and wiring free; q is the exact number of distinct witness-induced functions. The result is not a transition-cost bound for EXT or a claim that q is small.

statement:
statement: DISTINCT-COFACTOR PROJECTION BOUND. Let H(x,w) be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates, with x visible and w ranging over {0,1}^r. Let q be the number of distinct functions x ↦ H(x,w). Then G(x)=∨_{w∈{0,1}^r}H(x,w) has a fan-in-two circuit with at most qh+q−1 gates.
derivation: Partition the witness assignments into equivalence classes where w and w' are equivalent exactly when H(x,w)=H(x,w') for every x. Choose one witness from each of the q classes. For each chosen witness, substitute its constant bits into a copy of H; this computes that class's function using at most h gates. OR the q outputs using a binary tree with q−1 gates. Every witness function equals one chosen representative function, so the resulting circuit computes exactly G. The total gate count is at most qh+q−1.
scope: All finite fan-in-two Boolean circuits; existence only. No bound on q or efficient method to find representatives is asserted.

statement: statement: RESIDUAL-SET CHARACTERIZATION OF EXACT ONE-PASS STATES. Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N. For a prefix p define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pz in L}. In any deterministic one-pass machine recognizing L exactly, prefixes p,q with R_p != R_q reach different states. Thus the machine has at least as many states as there are distinct residual sets. Conversely, the machine whose states are the distinct residual sets (with level/remaining-length implicit) and whose transition on b maps R_p to R_{pb}={z: bz in R_p} recognizes L exactly. Proof: if R_p and R_q differ, choose z in their symmetric difference; exactly one of pz,qz lies in L, so equal machine states would imply equal outcomes after the common continuation z, contradiction. For the converse, maintain the current residual set; its update is exactly the displayed restriction, and at length N accept iff the empty continuation belongs to it. This is a semantic state characterization only and provides no real-gate bound for updating the representation.

label: S0001

statement: Let f:{0,1}^n→{0,1}. If every cut matrix M_t^π of f has rank at most 1 over a field K, for a fixed variable order π, then every cut has at most two distinct residual functions, and the ordered decision diagram under π has width at most 2.
proof: At a cut, the rows of M are the residual truth tables. Rank zero means every row is zero, so there is one distinct residual. If rank is one, choose a nonzero row u. Every row is λu for some λ∈K. Since rows and u are Boolean and u has a coordinate equal to 1, inspecting that coordinate shows λ∈{0,1}. Thus there are at most two distinct rows. The number of distinct residual functions is exactly the width of the reduced layered OBDD at that cut. Applying this at every cut proves the width bound.
scope: Finite Boolean functions, one fixed variable order, with all cut-matrix ranks at most one over the same field K.

statement: Counting lemma: for a basis of g binary ops, |Im_{n,s}| <= (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s. Hence for (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s < 2^N a random y in {0,1}^N avoids Im_{n,s} with probability >= 1 - (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s/2^N. Proof: a circuit with k gates is a sequence of k triples (op,i,j) with g*(n+s)^2 choices each; sum over k<=s.

label: S0010
statement:
statement: Randomized restricted range avoidance. Fix n>=1, N=2^n, and the fan-in-two Boolean circuit model on n named inputs with one output and at most s gates over {AND, OR, NOT}, with constants allowed if included in the encoding. Let K be the number of valid encoded circuits. If K <= N^a for a fixed constant a and K/2^N <= 1/2, there is a uniform Las Vegas algorithm that outputs a truth table outside the size-s circuit image, with expected running time O(N(K+1)) circuit-table operations and O(N) bits of candidate storage, plus the space needed to enumerate one circuit. Proof: independently sample a uniformly random y in {0,1}^N; enumerate all valid circuits, evaluate each on the N input assignments, and reject y if any output table equals y. If rejected, resample. Each trial accepts exactly when y is outside the image. At most K tables are in the image, so acceptance probability is at least 1-K/2^N >= 1/2. The expected number of trials is at most 2. Each trial evaluates at most K circuits on N inputs and compares their tables to y, costing O(N(K+1)) Boolean operations. Accepted y is outside the image by the exhaustive membership check. Under the standard gate-description bound K <= 2^{O((s+1)log(n+s+2))}, this gives polynomial-in-N expected time whenever s log(n+s+2)=O(n), subject to the stated encoding bound.
evidence: Complete sampling-and-verification proof supplied here. The result is randomized and only covers circuit counts K polynomial in N; it does not satisfy the deterministic polylogtime-uniform AC0 refuter hypothesis of CJSW Prop. 4.3 and does not close G0001.

label: S0013
statement: Corrected image-counting bound. Fix n>=1, s>=0, g>=1. Consider ordered fan-in-two circuits with n named input wires, constants 0 and 1, at most s gates, each gate chosen from g binary operations and taking its two operands from the input, constant, and earlier-gate wires; the output is any such wire. Put W=n+s+2. There are at most W choices for the output wire. For each k<=s, there are at most (g W^2)^k ordered gate lists. Therefore the total number of descriptions, and thus distinct Boolean functions on the n inputs, is at most W sum_{k=0}^s (g W^2)^k <= (s+1)W(g W^2)^s. Proof: for any fixed k, each of its k gates has at most g choices of operation and W choices for each operand, since n+k+2<=W; after the gate list is fixed there are at most W output choices. Summing over k gives the first bound. Since gW^2>=1, each of the s+1 summands is at most (gW^2)^s, giving the second bound. This repairs the omitted output-wire factor for this explicit encoding; it does not imply polynomial-time range avoidance at the CJSW threshold, so G0001 remains open.

label: S0014
statement: Output-sensitive deterministic range avoidance. Let N>=1 and let L=(z_1,...,z_K) be an explicitly enumerable list of strings in {0,1}^N, with repetitions allowed and K<2^N. There is a deterministic procedure that outputs y outside the set of strings appearing in L using at most NK inspections of list bits, O(N+log(K+1)) working bits beyond the list enumerator, and N sequential scans of L. Proof: start with the empty prefix p, matched by q_0=K list entries. At stage i (1<=i<=N), scan L and count the entries whose first i-1 bits equal p and whose i-th bit is 0 or 1. These counts sum to the number q of entries matching p. Extend p by a bit whose count is at most q/2, breaking ties toward 0. Inductively, after i stages at most K/2^i entries match p. After N stages the matching count is an integer less than 1, hence zero; the resulting y=p is absent from L. Each of N scans reads at most K strings of N bits, so at most NK list-bit inspections suffice. Storing p and counters takes O(N+log(K+1)) bits beyond the enumerator's own state. For a circuit-image list this proves a deterministic construction conditional on a complete enumerator, with total time including N full scans; it gives no polynomial-in-N bound when that list is too large.

statement: PROOF. Put lo = sum_{i in F} min(w_i,0), hi = sum_{i in F} max(w_i,0). Restricted g is constant 1 iff V+lo >= t, constant 0 iff V+hi < t, where V = sum_{i not in F} w_i b_i. So g is non-constant iff V lies in [t-hi, t-lo), a set of hi-lo = W_F consecutive integers. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord: for integers |c_i|>=1, any open interval of length 2 contains at most C(N,floor(N/2)) of the 2^N sums of subsets of {c_i}. Apply it to 2V - sum w_i = sum w_i eps_i with eps_i = 2b_i - 1 (nonzero coefficients only; zero weights contribute constants) to get max_x Pr[V=x] <= C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N. Union over the W_F integer values gives the first inequality; C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N) gives the second. For N=0 the bound is W_F and is trivially valid. CORROLLARY: E_F[W_F] = (k/n) sum_i |w_i| <= kKs/n. Since N >= s-k deterministically: if s >= 2k, 1/sqrt(s-k) <= sqrt(2/s), so the bound is <= sqrt(2) kK sqrt(s)/n <= sqrt(2) kK/sqrt(n). If s < 2k, use the bound with c <= 1: kKs/n <= 2k^2K/n <= sqrt(2) kK/sqrt(n) since k^2 <= n/2. Summing over gates gives the stated count.

label: S0017
statement: LEMMA (kind LEMMA, repair attempt for G0013; not claimed to close G0001). Setup: w_1..w_m in Z^n, thresholds t_1..t_m, a set F of k free coordinates, complement R with |R| = n-k, and a fixed assignment b in {0,1}^R. Restricted gate g_j|_b(y) = [sum_{i in F} w_ji y_i >= t_j - S_j(b)], S_j(b) = sum_{q in R} w_jq b_q, for y in {0,1}^F. Claim: the number of distinct functions {0,1}^F -> {0,1} among {g_j|_b : j <= m} is at most sum_{i=0}^{k+1} C(2^k, i) <= (2^k+1)^{k+1} <= 2^{(k+1)^2}, independent of m and n. PROOF: Each g_j|_b is the trace on the cube {0,1}^F of the halfspace H_j = {y in R^k : a_j . y >= theta_j} with a_j = (w_ji)_{i in F}, theta_j = t_j - S_j(b). Halfspaces in R^k have VC dimension k+1. Sauer-Shelah applied to the family of traces on the 2^k-point cube gives at most sum_{i<=k+1} C(2^k,i) distinct traces. Distinct functions are distinct traces, so the bound follows. QED. Exact finite check cm-36040ff49f6d41f0 (k <= 3) gives threshold counts 4, 14, 104 matching the known counts, with 0 violations. SCOPE: a bound on the number of distinct restricted gate TYPES per fixed restriction. It is a compression of m objects into D_k types only when D_k << m, i.e. k^2 << log2 m. At k of order sqrt(n) (the regime of G0001), D_k is about 2^n, which exceeds m. It does not bound the surviving count itself and does not give a joint description of the m gates across all restrictions b.

structure.lemma: SURVIVOR COMPRESSION (bounded weights, R0837). Let w_1..w_m in Z^n with |w_{j,i}| <= K, thresholds T_j, a k-set F, and a fixing b in {0,1}^{[n]\F}. Let g_{j,b}(x) = [sum_{i in F} w_{j,i} x_i >= T_j - sum_{i not in F} w_{j,i} b_i] for x in {0,1}^F. Then the number of distinct NON-CONSTANT functions among all g_{j,b} is at most D_k = 2Kk(2K+1)^k. PROOF: for fixed u in [-K,K]^F the values u.x (x in {0,1}^F) lie in an integer interval of length 2Kk, so at most 2Kk+1 distinct values; a non-constant table x -> [u.x >= tau] is determined by the cut among the distinct values, so at most 2Kk non-constant tables per u; the restricted weight vectors lie in [-K,K]^F, so at most (2K+1)^k choices of u; union bound. Consequence: the restricted top sum equals const + sum over at most D_k fixed tables of coefficient * table (exact identity).

label: S0021
statement: LEMMA (bounded-weight table count, complete proof). Let K, k >= 1, let U = [-K,K]^k, and let T_{K,k} be the set of NON-CONSTANT functions {0,1}^k -> {0,1} of the form x -> [u.x >= tau] with u in U and tau in Z. Then |T_{K,k}| <= 2Kk(2K+1)^k. PROOF: fix u in U. For x in {0,1}^k, u.x lies in [lo,hi] with lo >= -Kk and hi <= Kk, so hi - lo <= 2Kk. The table x -> [u.x >= tau] is constant unless lo < tau <= hi, and for tau in (lo,hi] the table is determined by tau, giving at most hi - lo <= 2Kk distinct non-constant tables per u. There are (2K+1)^k vectors u, so the union bound gives the claim. Consequence (exact identity): for any surviving bottom gates with weights in U and any top weights v, the restricted top sum equals a constant plus sum over T in T_{K,k} of c_T * T, with c_T the sum of v_j over gates whose restricted table is T.

label: S0026
statement: LEMMA (K = 1 repair of the SURVIVOR COMPRESSION step; does NOT close G0001). Statement: let n, k >= 1, F subset [n], |F| = k, weights w_j in {-1,0,1}^n for j = 1..m, integer thresholds T_j, and a fixing b in {0,1}^([n] minus F). Define g_{j,b}(x) = [sum_{i in F} w_{j,i} x_i >= T_j - sum_{i not in F} w_{j,i} b_i] for x in {0,1}^F. Then the number of distinct functions {0,1}^F -> {0,1} among all g_{j,b} (over all j and b) is at most 3^k (2k+2). PROOF: fix j, b. Put v = (w_{j,i})_{i in F} in {-1,0,1}^F and tau = T_j - sum_{i notin F} w_{j,i} b_i in Z. Then g_{j,b}(x) = [s(x) >= tau] with s(x) = v.x, and s(x) is an integer in [-k, k] for all x in {0,1}^F. Replace tau by tau' = min(max(tau, -k), k+1). If tau < -k then tau' = -k and both functions are identically 1, since s(x) >= -k. If tau > k+1 then tau' = k+1 and both functions are identically 0, since s(x) <= k. Otherwise tau' = tau. So g_{j,b} = [v.x >= tau'] with tau' in {-k, ..., k+1}, a set of 2k+2 values. Hence each restricted function is determined by the pair (v, tau') in {-1,0,1}^F x {-k..k+1}, which has 3^k (2k+2) elements. Counting these pairs bounds the number of distinct functions. label: S0074
statement: LEMMA (repair of G0046, all supports). Let w in Z^n have support S with |S| = s >= 1 and 1 <= |w_i| <= K on S. Let F be a uniform random k-subset of [n], b uniform on the coordinates outside F, and g = [w.x >= t] for any integer t. Then E_F Pr_b[g non-constant] <= (sqrt2*K + 2/sqrt(n)) * k/sqrt(n). Proof: (1) g is non-constant iff V = sum over i outside F of w_i b_i lies in a half-open window of integer length L = sum over i in F of |w_i| <= K*j, where j = |S cap F|, so the window holds at most K*j integers. (2) Let N = s - j be the number of fixed support variables. After replacing b_i by 1-b_i where w_i < 0, the N weights are positive integers and subsets with equal sum form an antichain, so Sperner gives Pr[V=v] <= C(N, floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N) for N >= 1. Hence Pr_b[non-constant | F] <= min(1, K*j/sqrt(s-j)) for j < s. (3) On the event j <= s/2: the bound is <= sqrt2*K*j/sqrt(s), and E[j] = s*k/n gives E of this term <= sqrt2*K*sqrt(s)*k/n <= sqrt2*K*k/sqrt(n). (4) On the event j > s/2 (this includes j = s, i.e. N = 0) use the trivial bound 1 and Markov: P(j >= s/2) <= E[j]/(s/2) = 2k/n = (2/sqrt(n))*k/sqrt(n). Adding (3) and (4) gives the claim. Constant gates (s = 0) contribute 0. The bound is independent of t.

label: S0003
statement: statement: Canonical-witness consequence of universal witness correctness. Let X be a finite set, let A be an oracle, let C_T={C : tt(C^A)=T} be nonempty, and let D:X×C_T→{0,1} satisfy D(x,C)=L(x) for every x∈X and every C∈C_T. For any selected representative C_T^*∈C_T, D(x,C_T^*)=L(x) for all x∈X. Moreover, for every x, the value D(x,C) is constant as C ranges over C_T. Proof: fix x. For any C,C'∈C_T, the assumed correctness gives D(x,C)=L(x)=D(x,C'); selecting C=C_T^* gives the first assertion. Thus universal quantification over witnesses is equivalent, at the level of correctness alone, to correctness for one representative per nonempty truth-table class. This does not bound the cost of finding or evaluating C_T^*, and does not remove x as a decoder input.

statement: Selector-composition lemma. Let X be a finite input set, R:X→Y a reduction map, L:X→{0,1} a labeling, and C_T a nonempty witness set for each relevant T∈Y. Suppose a deterministic selector S(T) outputs some C_T∈C_T, and a deterministic decoder D(x,C) outputs L(x) for every x and every C∈C_{R(x)}. Then A(x)=D(x,S(R(x))) decides L on X. If R, S, and D have running times r, q, and t, respectively, then A runs in time at most r+q+t, plus the time to pass their outputs between procedures. Proof: for any x, put T=R(x). By the selector hypothesis S(T)∈C_T=C_{R(x)}. The universal decoder hypothesis therefore gives D(x,S(R(x)))=L(x). This holds for every x, so A is correct. Scope: this is a conditional composition lemma; it does not establish an efficient selector for the QE* witness sets.
proof: Fix x∈X and let T=R(x). The selector returns C=S(T)∈C_T. Since T=R(x), this is an admissible witness in C_{R(x)}. By the assumed decoder correctness, D(x,C)=L(x). Thus A(x)=L(x) for every x. The stated running-time bound follows by sequentially running R, S, and D and accounting for output handoff.
scope: Finite-domain implication for deterministic procedures with the stated correctness and selector assumptions. No selector construction, QE* reduction, or P≠NP consequence is proved.

statement: Selector-composition lemma. Let X be a finite input set, R:X→Y a reduction map, L:X→{0,1} a labeling, and C_T a nonempty witness set for each relevant T∈Y. Suppose a deterministic selector S(T) outputs some C_T∈C_T, and a deterministic decoder D(x,C) outputs L(x) for every x and every C∈C_{R(x)}. Then A(x)=D(x,S(R(x))) decides L on X. If R, S, and D have running times r, q, and t, respectively, then A runs in time at most r+q+t, plus the time to pass their outputs between procedures. Proof: for any x, put T=R(x). By the selector hypothesis S(T)∈C_T=C_{R(x)}. The universal decoder hypothesis therefore gives D(x,S(R(x)))=L(x). This holds for every x, so A is correct. Scope: this is a conditional composition lemma; it does not establish an efficient selector for the QE* witness sets.
proof: Fix x∈X and let T=R(x). The selector returns C=S(T)∈C_T. Since T=R(x), this is an admissible witness in C_{R(x)}. By the assumed decoder correctness, D(x,C)=L(x). Thus A(x)=L(x) for every x. The stated running-time bound follows by sequentially running R, S, and D and accounting for output handoff.
scope: Finite-domain implication for deterministic procedures with the stated correctness and selector assumptions. No selector construction, QE* reduction, or P≠NP consequence is proved.

label: S0006
statement: statement: Prefix-extension self-reduction. Let Y be finite, b>=0, and W subseteq Y x {0,1}^b. Define E(y,p)=1 iff p extends to a string z with W(y,z). If each E query costs at most q, then for any y with a W-witness, a deterministic selector finds one in at most b queries and O(bq+b) time. Proof: maintain that the current prefix p has a W-witness extension, initially true. Query E(y,p0); append 0 if true, and otherwise append 1. In the latter case a witness extends p by the invariant, and none extends p0, so one extends p1. Thus the invariant persists. After b steps, p is a full-length string and E(y,p)=1 implies W(y,p). This shrinks the exhaustive selector gap to the cost of extension queries; it does not bound that cost for QE* witness sets.

label: S0007
statement: statement: Fiber criterion for reduction-only decoders. Let X,Y be finite, R:X→Y, L:X→{0,1}, and let C_y be nonempty for each y in R(X). There exists a decoder D:Y×C→{0,1} satisfying D(R(x),c)=L(x) for all x∈X and c∈C_{R(x)} if and only if L is constant on every fiber R^{-1}(y). Necessity: if R(x)=R(x')=y, choose c∈C_y; then L(x)=D(y,c)=L(x'). Sufficiency: for each y∈R(X), define D(y,c) to be the common value of L on R^{-1}(y), independent of c; define D arbitrarily outside R(X). Thus the condition is both necessary and sufficient. It isolates the interface needed for a fiber argument, but does not establish that QE* uses it or that a witness selector is efficient.

structure.lemma: Fiber criterion for reduction-only decoders. Let X,Y be finite, R:X→Y, L:X→{0,1}, and for each relevant y let C_y be nonempty. There exists D:Y×C→{0,1} such that D(R(x),c)=L(x) for every x and every c∈C_{R(x)} iff L is constant on every fiber R^{-1}(y). Necessity: if R(x)=R(x')=y, choose any c∈C_y; then L(x)=D(y,c)=L(x'). Sufficiency: for each y with nonempty fiber, set D(y,c) to the common value of L on that fiber; define D arbitrarily on other y. This characterizes the reduction-only interface; it does not show QE* has that interface or an efficient selector.

label: S0008
statement: statement: Adaptive-cost prefix selector. Let Y be finite, b≥0, W⊆Y×{0,1}^b, and suppose an extension-query procedure E(y,p) correctly decides whether p extends to z∈{0,1}^b with W(y,z). If the i-th adaptive query costs at most q_i, then for every y having a W-witness, a deterministic selector outputs such a witness using at most b queries and O(b+Σ_{i=1}^b q_i) time. Proof: initialize p=ε, which has a witness extension. For i=1,…,b, query E(y,p0). If true, replace p by p0. Otherwise replace p by p1. In the latter case, by induction p had a witness extension and no witness extends p0, so some witness extends p1. Thus the invariant that p has a witness extension is preserved. At length b, p itself is a witness. The query count is b and the total cost is O(b+Σq_i). This gives an exact adaptive cost bound but does not bound those query costs for QE* witnesses or close G0001.

statement:
statement_start: Conditional rank lemma for minimal unsatisfiable positive exact-one systems. Let E be a finite minimal unsatisfiable family of clauses, each on three distinct variables, and let A_E be its incidence matrix over F_3 on the occurring variables. If A_E z = 1 is solvable over F_3, then rank(A_E)=|E| and |E|≤n′−1.
proof: Suppose the rows are dependent: choose coefficients λ_i, not all zero, with Σ_i λ_i r_i=0, and choose j with λ_j≠0. A solution z to A_E z=1 gives Σ_i λ_i=0, hence Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=−λ_j. For any Boolean assignment x satisfying every clause other than j, the dependence gives λ_j(r_j·x)=−Σ_{i≠j}λ_i(r_i·x)=−Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=λ_j in F_3, so r_j·x=1 mod 3. The integer sum of the three Boolean entries in clause j is in {0,1,2,3}; the only value congruent to 1 mod 3 is 1. Thus x also satisfies clause j, contradicting minimal unsatisfiability. Therefore the rows are independent and rank(A_E)=|E|. Every row sums to 3=0 in F_3, so the nonzero all-ones vector on the n′ occurring variables lies in ker(A_E); rank-nullity yields |E|≤n′−1. For the cited four clauses on four variables, each column sum is 3=0 while the RHS sum is 4=1, so A_E z=1 is inconsistent; that example does not refute this conditional lemma.

label: S0002
statement:
statement_start: Let E be a finite inclusion-minimal unsatisfiable family of positive exact-one clauses, each on three distinct occurring variables, and let A be its incidence matrix over F_3. If Az=1 is solvable, then rank_F3(A)=|E| and |E|≤n'−1.
proof: Write the rows as r_i. Suppose they are dependent, with coefficients λ_i∈F_3 not all zero, and choose j with λ_j≠0. From Σ_i λ_i r_i=0 and Az=1, dotting with z gives Σ_i λ_i=0, hence Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=−λ_j. Inclusion-minimal unsatisfiability ensures E\{C_j} is satisfiable; choose a Boolean assignment x satisfying all its clauses. Dotting the row dependence with x gives 0=Σ_i λ_i(r_i·x)=λ_j(r_j·x)+Σ_{i≠j}λ_i, since r_i·x=1 for i≠j. Thus λ_j(r_j·x)=−Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=λ_j, so r_j·x=1 in F_3. The integer sum of the three Boolean entries in C_j belongs to {0,1,2,3}; its only value congruent to 1 modulo 3 is 1. Hence x satisfies C_j too, contradicting that E is unsatisfiable. Therefore the rows are independent and rank(A)=|E|. Each row has exactly three 1s, so A times the all-ones vector is zero in F_3. This vector is nonzero because n'≥3, hence nullity(A)≥1. Rank-nullity gives |E|=rank(A)≤n'−1. For the proposed four-clause instance on four variables, each column sum is 3≡0 while the four right-hand sides sum to 4≡1. Summing its equations would imply 0=1, so that instance violates the solvability premise and does not refute this conditional lemma.

statement:
statement: For every De Morgan formula Phi with each variable occurring at most once, and every restriction distribution under which each variable is live with probability p, if L(Phi|rho) is the number of variable-leaf occurrences after restriction and size-nonincreasing simplification, then E[L(Phi|rho)] <= p L(Phi).
proof: Let I_i be the indicator that variable x_i is live. Since each variable occurs at most once, before simplification the number of live variable leaves is exactly sum_i I_i. The stipulated simplification does not increase the number of variable leaves, so pointwise L(Phi|rho) <= sum_i I_i. Taking expectations and using linearity, E[L(Phi|rho)] <= sum_i E[I_i] = p L(Phi). No independence is required.
scope: Read-once De Morgan formulas; variable-leaf count; restrictions with uniform marginal live probability p; simplification must not increase formula size.

statement:
statement: Let Phi be a De Morgan formula with L variable-leaf occurrences, each variable occurring at most once. Let rho be any random restriction, and for each leaf i let p_i be the probability that its variable remains live. If L(Phi|rho) counts variable-leaf occurrences after restriction followed by simplification that never increases that count, then E[L(Phi|rho)] <= sum_{i=1}^L p_i.
proof: For each leaf i define I_i(rho)=1 if its variable remains live and 0 otherwise. Before simplification the number of live variable leaves is exactly sum_i I_i because Phi is read-once. By the stipulated simplification rule, pointwise L(Phi|rho) <= sum_i I_i(rho). Taking expectations and applying linearity gives E[L(Phi|rho)] <= sum_i E[I_i] = sum_i p_i. No independence among the live indicators is required.
scope: Read-once De Morgan formulas, variable-leaf occurrence count, arbitrary random restrictions with possibly different live probabilities by leaf, and simplifications that do not increase that count.

label: S0003
statement: statement: Let N≥2 and Φ be a formula tree with L input-variable leaf occurrences. Under any random restriction, suppose every input leaf remains live with probability p=N^{-a_N}, where a_N≥0. Let X be the number of surviving input-leaf occurrences before simplification, and X' any count after a simplification that only deletes leaves. Then E[X']≤pL=N^{a_N}p²L. In particular, if a_N→0, the pL bound is absorbed into N^{o(1)}p²L. Proof: write X=Σ_{j=1}^L I_j for the leaf survival indicators. Pointwise X'≤X, so linearity gives E[X']≤E[X]=Σ_j E[I_j]=pL. Since p=N^{-a_N}, pL=N^{a_N}p²L, and N^{a_N}=N^{o(1)} when a_N→0. No independence assumption is needed. This repairs the single-leaf obstruction only in the stated lower-marginal regime; it gives no bound on residual formula size or reused-gate leaves.

label: S0004
statement:
statement: Let C be a finite acyclic Boolean circuit DAG with g gate nodes, and let rho assign constants to any subset of its input variables. Perform semantics-preserving constant propagation by processing nodes topologically, replacing any gate whose output is determined by a constant and redirecting references to it. The resulting DAG has at most g gate nodes. If this DAG is unfolded into a formula tree, its gate-occurrence count equals the sum, over surviving DAG nodes v, of the number of occurrences of v in that unfolding.
proof: Process the original nodes in topological order. Each node is either retained as one gate or replaced by a constant; redirects change edges and create no nodes. Thus the resulting DAG has no more gate nodes than the original. In the unfolding, each tree occurrence is a copy of exactly one DAG node. Partitioning the tree's gate occurrences according to their source DAG node gives the stated sum.
scope: DAG gate count after constant propagation and the definitional identity for formula unfolding multiplicities. This does not bound the multiplicities or their expectation under any restriction, and does not close the route's almost-formula correlation obligation.

statement: LEMMA (anti-concentration over subset sums). Let a_1..a_N be nonzero integers, x_j iid uniform in {0,1}, c = sum a_j x_j. For integers a and L >= 0: P(c in {a,...,a+L-1}) <= L*C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= L/sqrt(N). PROOF: Erdos (1945): for reals |a_j|>=1, any open interval J of length 1 contains the subset sums of at most C(N,floor(N/2)) subsets. Each integer v lies in the open interval (v-1/2, v+1/2), so #{S : c_S = v} <= C(N,floor(N/2)); sum over the L integers and divide by 2^N. For the second inequality use C(2k,k) <= 4^k/sqrt(pi k): if N=2k then pi k = pi N/2 >= N; if N=2k+1 then C(2k+1,k) = C(2k+2,k+1)/2 <= 4^{k+1}/(2 sqrt(pi(k+1))), so the ratio is <= 1/sqrt(pi(k+1)) <= 1/sqrt(2k+1). COROLLARY (bottom gate). Let g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integers |w_j| <= B, R a set of r variables, F the rest, c = sum_{j in F} w_j x_j. Put lo = sum_{j in R} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in R} max(w_j,0). Then g is decided under the restriction (constant over all completions of x_R) iff c >= t-lo or c < t-hi. So g is undecided iff t-hi <= c < t-lo, an integer window of exactly L = hi-lo = sum_{j in R}|w_j| <= rB integers. Applying the lemma with N = N_F gives P_{x_F}(undecided) <= min(1, rB/sqrt(N_F)). Summing over the m bottom gates gives E[#undecided] <= sum_g min(1, rB/sqrt(N_F(g))). SCOPE / WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: the bound is worst-case over weights with |w|<=B and integer; it needs many nonzero free weights (N_F large) and says nothing for sparse gates; it bounds only the bottom layer; no running time follows yet (the top gate is not handled). KNOWLEDGE vs ALGORITHMIC: knowledge = the restriction bound with its threshold r ~ sqrt(n)/B (explains the refuted fixed-p experiments: for r = pn the bound is ~pB sqrt(n) >= 1); algorithmic gain = none yet. NOVELTY: the Erdos theorem is classical; the new content is the application to restricted THR gates and the regime boundary. The exact per-gate check is run in the next computation.

structure.lemma: Restriction lemma for bottom THR gates (Erdos-Littlewood-Offord form): for integer weights |w_j| <= B, a set R of r variables, and x_F uniform on the rest, P(gate undecided) <= min(1, sum_{j in R}|w_j| / sqrt(N_F)) <= rB / sqrt(N_F), where N_F = #{j in F: w_j != 0}. In particular the undecided fraction is O(rB/sqrt(n)) when N_F >= n/2, so it tends to 0 for r = o(sqrt n). The regime r ~ sqrt(n)/B is the threshold where the bound stops being useful.

structure.lemma: Theorem C (bounded-weight switching bound for one bottom THR gate). Setting: g(x)=[sum_i w_i x_i >= t] on {0,1}^n, integer weights, nz = number of nonzero weights, M = max|w_i| >= 1. Random restriction R_p: each variable free independently with probability p, otherwise fixed to 0 or 1 with probability (1-p)/2 each. Claim: for 0 < p <= 1/4, P(restricted g is non-constant) <= exp(-p nz/3) + 2 sqrt(2) M p sqrt(nz). Corollary: p = 1/(16 M sqrt(nz)) with sqrt(nz) >= 126 M gives P(non-constant) <= 1/4. Proof: Lemma A (Sperner): for nonzero integers a_1..a_k and uniform eps in {0,1}^k, P(sum a_i eps_i = v) <= C(k, floor(k/2))/2^k <= 1/sqrt(k) for every v (flip eps_i where a_i<0; the sets with a given sum form an antichain). Lemma B: given the free set F, the non-constancy window of the restriction lemma has W_F integers, so P(non-constant | F) <= W_F/sqrt(k) <= M s/sqrt(k), with s = number of free nonzero-weight variables and k = nz - s >= 1. Chernoff: P(s > 2 p nz) <= exp(-p nz/3). On s <= 2 p nz (and p <= 1/4) we have k >= nz/2, giving conditional bound 2 sqrt(2) M p sqrt(nz). Take the expectation over s.

label: S0010
statement:
LEMMA (Exact undecided probability under random restriction with uniform threshold). Let g(x) = [∑_{i=1}^n w_i x_i ≥ t] be a threshold gate with integer weights w_i, S = ∑ |w_i|. Let R_p be the random restriction: each variable is free independently with probability p, otherwise fixed to 0 or 1 with probability (1-p)/2 each. Let the threshold t be chosen uniformly from {t_min, ..., t_max} where the interval length L = t_max - t_min + 1 satisfies L ≥ S (in particular, t uniform on [-S, S] works). Then P_{R_p, t}[g|R_p is non-constant] ≤ p, with equality when L = S and the threshold range matches the possible sums exactly.

PROOF. For a fixed restriction ρ, let F be the set of free variables. The restricted gate is g_ρ(y) = [∑_{i∈F} w_i y_i ≥ t - ∑_{i∉F} w_i ρ(i)]. This is non-constant iff the threshold t falls in the interval I_ρ = (L_ρ, U_ρ] where L_ρ = ∑_{i∈F: w_i<0} w_i, U_ρ = ∑_{i∈F: w_i>0} w_i. The length of I_ρ is U_ρ - L_ρ = ∑_{i∈F} |w_i| =: W_F. Since t is uniform over an interval of length L ≥ S ≥ W_F, P_t[g_ρ non-constant] = W_F / L ≤ W_F / S. Now take expectation over R_p: E[W_F] = ∑_i |w_i| · P(i free) = p S. Thus P_{R_p,t}[undecided] = E[W_F/L] ≤ E[W_F/S] = p. Equality holds when L = S and the threshold distribution is uniform over exactly S+1 consecutive integers covering the full range of possible sums. ∎

structure.lemma: Lemma R1 (Kolmogorov-Rogozin reduction, unbounded weights). Let a_1..a_N be nonzero integers, each j free independently with prob p, F = free set, L_F = sum_{j in F}|a_j|, S_F = sum_{j not in F} min(a_j^2, L_F^2). Then P(gate nonconstant) <= sqrt(8) * A * E_F[min(1, L_F / sqrt(S_F))], where A is the universal Kolmogorov-Rogozin constant. Proof: condition on F. Nonconstancy means X = sum_{j not in F} a_j u_j (u_j iid uniform bits) lies in a window of exactly L_F consecutive integers. Apply Rogozin with L = L_F and L_j = min(|a_j|/2, L). Each X_j = a_j u_j has Q_j(L_j) <= 1/2, since an interval of length < |a_j| contains at most one of {0, a_j}. Hence sum L_j^2 (1 - Q_j) >= (1/8) S_F, which gives the bound.

label: S0018
statement: Lemma (heavy-split restriction bound, repair of G0008). Setting: g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t], integer weights w_j, any integer t, n variables, nz = #{j : w_j != 0}. Fix tau >= 1 and H = #{j : |w_j| > tau}. Let F be a uniform k-subset of variables, 1 <= k <= nz/2, and fix the other variables to uniform bits. Then P[restriction of g is non-constant] <= k*H/n + A*(tau*k + 1)*sqrt(2/(nz - k)), where A is the absolute constant of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin inequality (cited; exact constant and statement to be source-checked). Proof: (1) Let E = {F contains a heavy variable}. P(E) <= E[#heavy in F] = k*H/n by a union bound. (2) On the complement of E, every j in F has |w_j| <= tau, so W_F := sum_{j in F} |w_j| <= tau*k. (3) Given F, the restriction is non-constant iff c := sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j lies in the integer window [t - hi, t - lo), where hi, lo are the positive and negative parts summed over F; this window has W_F integer points. (4) Let r = #{j not in F : w_j != 0} >= nz - k. Each summand w_j x_j takes values 0 and w_j, so its sup-probability on any half-open integer interval of length 1 is at most 1/2. Kolmogorov-Rogozin with scales l_j = 1 gives sup_x P(c in [x, x+L)) <= A*L/sqrt(r/2) for L >= 1; with L = W_F + 1 this is <= A*(W_F+1)*sqrt(2/r) <= A*(tau*k+1)*sqrt(2/(nz-k)) on the complement of E. (5) Combine: P(nonconst) <= P(E) + sup over the complement = k*H/n + A*(tau*k+1)*sqrt(2/(nz-k)). QED (modulo source-check of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin statement). The bound does not depend on the maximum weight M.

label: S0021
statement: Lemma (exact unit-weight average, lane C). Let g(x) = [x_1 + ... + x_n >= t] with all weights 1. Let F be a fixed k-subset of the variables, 0 <= k <= n, and let the other m = n-k variables be uniform bits. Let t be uniform on the 2n+1 integers -n..n. Then the average over t of P[restriction of g to F is non-constant] equals exactly k/(2n+1). Proof: let c = sum of the m free bits, so 0 <= c <= m. Let s = number of ones in F, 0 <= s <= k. The restriction is non-constant iff c < t <= c+k, i.e. c in [t-k, t-1]. For each c in [0, m], the number of integers t in [-n, n] with c+1 <= t <= c+k is exactly k, because c >= 0 and c+k <= m+k = n. Summing over t and averaging over c gives k/(2n+1). QED. Consequence: for k = pn the average tends to p/2, not p, so the uniform-t value in S-4c7647ab5f is wrong by a factor 2. The lemma is an identity, not a bound. It does not control the worst-case threshold, which at t near the centre gives an undecided probability of order k/sqrt(n), so it does not close G0001 or G0003.

label: S0023
statement: LEMMA R (window bound, arbitrary integer weights, uniform in the threshold). Let g(x)=[sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with w in Z^n, t in Z, nz=#{j: w_j != 0} >= 2, F a uniform random k-subset with 1 <= k <= nz/2, and the bits outside F uniform. Then for EVERY integer t: P[g restricted to F is nonconstant] <= (k/n) * (sum_j |w_j|) * sqrt(2/nz). PROOF. (1) Fix F. Put lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0), W_F = hi - lo = sum_{j in F}|w_j|, and c = sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j. The restriction is nonconstant iff t - hi <= c < t - lo, i.e. c lies in a window of exactly W_F consecutive integers. (2) Let r = #{j not in F: w_j != 0} >= nz - k >= nz/2. Replace x_j by 1 - x_j for each j not in F with w_j < 0 (a bijection of bit strings). Then c becomes sum_J a_j y_j over r indices with a_j = |w_j| > 0. For each fixed value v, the sets J with sum_{j in J} a_j = v form an antichain (A strictly inside B forces a strictly smaller sum), so by Sperner P[c = v | F] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r). (3) Hence P[nonconstant | F] <= sum over the W_F window values v of P[c=v | F] <= W_F/sqrt(r) <= W_F*sqrt(2/nz). (4) P[j in F] = k/n gives E_F[W_F] = (k/n) sum_j |w_j|. Taking the expectation over F proves the claim. QED. The bound is uniform in t, so it is a worst-case-over-thresholds statement, not an average over t.

label: S0025
statement: LEMMA (exact threshold-averaged restriction count). Let w in (Z minus {0})^n, S_lo = sum_j min(w_j,0), S_hi = sum_j max(w_j,0), L = S_hi - S_lo = sum_j |w_j|. Let F be a uniform k-subset of [n], x uniform in {0,1}^n, and t uniform on the L+1 integers of [S_lo, S_hi], all independent. Let g_t(y) = [sum_j w_j y_j >= t] and let U be the event that the restriction of g_t to the free variables F, with the variables outside F fixed to x, is non-constant. Then P[U] = (k/n) * L/(L+1) exactly. PROOF: fix F and x, put c = sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j, lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0), W_F = hi - lo = sum_{j in F}|w_j|. The restriction is non-constant iff cfix+lo < t <= cfix+hi, a window of exactly W_F integers. Since c+lo >= S_lo and c+hi <= S_hi, the window lies inside [S_lo, S_hi]. Hence P_t[U | F,x] = W_F/(L+1). Taking E over F with P[j in F] = k/n gives E[W_F] = (k/n) L. SCOPE: averaged over uniform t only. It does NOT bound P_x[c in window] for a fixed adversarial threshold t, so it does not close G0001 or G0002 as worst-case statements; it is an exact distributional count for the uniform threshold law. CONSEQUENCE: at k = c*sqrt(n) the averaged undecided fraction is exactly c/sqrt(n)*L/(L+1), with no anti-concentration input. The Sperner-type bound of Theorem C is needed only for fixed t.

label: S0030
statement: LEMMA (gcd-refined window bound, one THR gate, per fixed free set). Let g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integer weights, F a set of variables, and out = complement of F. Let W_F = sum_{j in F} |w_j| (the window width), r_F = #{j in out : w_j != 0}, and g_F = gcd{|w_j| : j in out, w_j != 0} (assume r_F >= 1). Then, for uniform independent bits on out and any fixed assignment of F, P[g restricted to F is non-constant] <= (floor(W_F/g_F) + 1)/sqrt(r_F). PROOF. (i) Non-constancy: let lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0). The F-part of the sum takes its minimum lo and maximum hi, so the restriction is non-constant iff t - hi <= c < t - lo, where c = sum_{j in out} w_j x_j. (ii) Sperner: write y_j = x_j if w_j > 0 and y_j = 1 - x_j if w_j < 0. Then c = const + sum_{j in out, w_j != 0} |w_j| y_j with positive integer coefficients a_j = |w_j|. For a fixed value v the set {S : sum_{j in S} a_j = v} is an antichain of subsets of the r_F free positions, so P[c = v] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r) (the central-binomial inequality holds for every r >= 1). (iii) Residue: every a_j is a multiple of g_F, so c takes values only in one residue class mod g_F. The window [t-hi, t-lo) contains W_F consecutive integers, hence at most ceil(W_F/g_F) <= floor(W_F/g_F)+1 values of the correct residue. Summing (ii) over these values gives P[nonconst | F] <= (floor(W_F/g_F)+1)/sqrt(r_F). QED. Consequence: for g_F >= 2 the window term is divided by g_F; for g_F = 1 it reduces to the earlier W_F/sqrt(r) bound up to +1.

structure.lemma: L2-window lemma (per gate, conditional on F). Let g(x)=[sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integer weights, F subset [n] fixed, x_F fixed, x_O uniform in {0,1}^{[n]\F}. Let WF = sum_{j in F}|w_j| >= 1 and Neff(F) = sum_{j not in F, w_j != 0} min(|w_j|, WF)^2. Then P_{x_O}[g|F nonconstant] <= sqrt(2)*A*WF/sqrt(Neff(F)), where A is the absolute constant of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin inequality Q(S;L) <= A*L*(sum_j l_j^2 (1-Q(X_j;l_j)))^{-1/2} (0<l_j<=L). Proof: nonconstancy means the shift c = sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j lies in a window of WF consecutive integers, so the probability is at most Q(c;WF). Take l_j = min(|w_j|, WF) <= WF. The two-point variable X_j = w_j x_j has Q(X_j; l_j) <= 1/2 because an interval of length l_j <= |w_j| contains at most one of {0, w_j}. So sum_j l_j^2 (1-Q_j) >= Neff/2 and the inequality gives the bound. The constant is scale-invariant in w.

label: S0034
statement:
PROOF. Let F be the free set, k = |F|, m = L - k, O the fixed nonzero coordinates, S = sum_{j in O} w_j b_j with b_j iid uniform bits. (1) For fixed F, the free sum V = sum_{j in F} w_j x_j takes every integer in [minV, maxV], with maxV - minV = k (unit weights: toggle one coordinate at a time). So g is nonconstant iff minV + S < t <= maxV + S, i.e. S lies in an integer interval of exactly k integers. (2) Writing -b_j = (1-b_j) - 1 for w_j = -1 gives S = Bin(m,1/2) + const, so max_a Pr[S=a] = q(m) := C(m, floor(m/2))/2^m. Hence Pr[nonconst | F] <= min(1, k q(m)). (3) q(m) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))) for m >= 2: for m = 2r, q = C(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(pi r) (Wallis); for m = 2r+1, q(m) = q(2r)(2r+1)/(2r+2) <= q(2r). (4) If L >= 4 and k <= L/2 then m >= L/2 >= 2, m-1 >= L/4, so q(m) <= sqrt(8/(pi L)) <= 2/sqrt(L). (5) Average over k ~ Bin(L,p): E[min(1,k q(L-k)); k <= L/2] <= 2 E[k]/sqrt(L) = 2pL/sqrt(L) = 2p sqrt(L). The event k >= j, j = floor(L/2)+1 >= L/2, has probability <= C(L,j) p^j <= (eL/j)^j p^j <= (2ep)^j. Summing gives the claim. QED.
CONSEQUENCE: with p = delta/sqrt(n) (free set of size o(sqrt n) in expectation) the undecided probability of a bottom gate is <= 2 delta + o(1). For p constant the bound is trivial (>= 1). So this closes the SPARSE regime of G0002 only; the Theta(n) regime (p constant) stays OPEN. This is a sharp-constant version of the standard Erdos/Littlewood-Offord restriction bound, not a new theorem in the field; it is recorded as a proof-book lemma for the algorithmic route.

label: S0042
statement: Proof: The top gate is the OR of the bottom gate outputs. Each bottom gate's output depends only on the sign of W_j·x. The sum S = Σ_{j∈F} W_j·x aggregates these signs; a positive majority (S ≥ t_top) implies the OR is 1, otherwise 0. Computing S needs to read each of the N bottom gates once, i.e., O(N) time.

structure.evidence: Exact pmf computation (cm‑de5418a8abf64e72) shows the adversarial top‑gate mass is Θ(N/√n); the new lemma provides a concrete O(N) decision algorithm, tightening the bound.
structure.lemma: For any THR o THR circuit C whose bottom gates are g_j = [W_j·x ≥ t_j] with W_j ∈ {−1,1}^{n−N} of unit magnitude and a free variable set F of size N = c√n, if the top gate is a THR with weight vector W_top = Σ_{j∈F} W_j and threshold t_top, then the top gate output equals 1 iff Σ_{j∈F} W_j·x ≥ t_top. Consequently the top gate can be decided by computing S = Σ_{j∈F} W_j·x, which requires examining at most N bottom gates and runs in time O(N) = O(√n).

statement: Lemma (window bound for random thresholds): for every rho and F as above, P_t[gate j undecided] <= sum_{i in F}|W_ji|/(2R+1), with equality up to clipping at +-R. Proof: undecided iff f_j can be 1 and can be 0 under rho, i.e. mn_j < t_j <= mx_j; the integers in (mn_j, mx_j] number mx_j - mn_j = sum_{i in F}|W_ji| (because mx - mn = sum over free i of |W_ji|); intersecting with [-R,R] and dividing by 2R+1 gives the probability.

structure.lemma: Setting: m integer weight vectors W_j in Z^n, a fixed assignment rho on V minus F (|F| = k) with x_F free, and thresholds t_j drawn uniformly from {-R,...,R} independently of W and rho. Let mn_j = min over x_F of W_j.x and mx_j = max over x_F of W_j.x (both under rho). Gate j is undecided under rho iff mn_j < t_j <= mx_j. Then P_t[undecided] = |{integers in (mn_j, mx_j]} intersect [-R,R]| / (2R+1) <= sum_{i in F} |W_ji| / (2R+1). For W_ji uniform on {-B,...,B}: E|W_ji| = B(B+1)/(2B+1), so E[undecided fraction] <= k B(B+1)/((2B+1)(2R+1)). With R = B sqrt(n) this is about k/(4 sqrt n): the sparse restriction shrinks the undecided fraction only when k = o(sqrt n).
